body:
### Motivation
- Add a self-contained mini runner game into the repository to provide an interactive demo/feature under `runner/`.
- Provide a simple local-run experience and make game assets replaceable via a central mapping.
- Track and persist local best scores to offer basic persistent state across sessions.

### Description
- Add `runner/index.html` which provides the game shell, HUD, start and game-over overlays, and links to the game script and styles.
- Add `runner/style.css` which implements layout, HUD, overlays, responsive behavior, and visual theming for the game.
- Add `runner/game.js` which implements the full game loop, input (keyboard and touch) handling, asset loading via `ASSET_PATHS`, spawning and behavior for obstacles and coins, collision detection, particle effects, pause/resume, and `localStorage`-backed best-score tracking.
- Add `runner/README.md` with local run instructions (`python3 -m http.server 4173`) and the list of required asset paths and how to update `ASSET_PATHS`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were added or run for this change.

author: khangnghiem
body:
Fix layers panel not populating on initial page load.

## Root Cause
The render loop's `refreshLayersPanel()` call was gated by `uiDirty && time - minimapLastRender > MINIMAP_INTERVAL`. While `uiDirty` starts as `true`, the interval check could prevent the first call. The panel remained empty until a user interaction set `uiDirty = true` again.

## Fix
- Add explicit `refreshLayersPanel()` + `renderMinimap()` calls in the deferred init timeout (100ms after WASM init)
- Bump cache-bust to v0.11.4 to ensure fix is served immediately

author: gooson
body:
### Motivation
- Watch templates with hyphenated IDs (e.g. `stair-climber`) and localized names (e.g. `스텝 클라이머`) were sometimes resolved to `.mixedCardio`, causing the Watch to show mixed/cardio UX while iPhone showed stair cardio.
- The goal is to make activity type resolution consistent across platforms so machine-level UI (level input) and cardio flows match between watch and iPhone.

### Description
- Normalize exercise IDs before name inference by converting `-`/`_` to spaces and re-running `WorkoutActivityType.infer`, implemented in `WorkoutActivityType.resolveCardioActivity` in `DUNE/Domain/Models/WorkoutActivityType.swift`.
- Expanded inference keyword table to include additional stair variants (`"step climber"`, `"stepclimber"`, `"스텝 클라이머"`, `"스텝클라이머"`) so localized and alternate names map to `.stairClimbing`.
- Added/updated unit tests in `DUNETests/WorkoutActivityTypeTests.swift` to cover the new keywords and a regression test verifying `resolveCardioActivity(from: "stair-climber", name: "스텝 클라이머", inputTypeRaw: "durationDistance")` yields `.stairClimbing`.

### Testing
- Unit tests were added to `DUNETests/WorkoutActivityTypeTests.swift` to exercise name inference and the ID-based resolution path and they compile locally in this workspace (tests added and file changes staged).
- Attempted to run the targeted test via `xcodebuild test -project DUNE/DUNE.xcodeproj -scheme DUNETests -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17,OS=26.2' -only-testing:DUNETests/WorkoutActivityTypeTests`, but the environment does not have `xcodebuild` installed so automated execution could not be performed here (command returned `command not found`).

Previous implementation assumed ViewTransitions was active. It was not imported in BaseLayout.

body:
This PR updates [chardet](https://pypi.org/project/chardet) from **4.0.0** to **7.1.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.1.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Added PEP 263 encoding declaration detection — `` -*- coding: ... -*-``
  and `` coding=...`` declarations on lines 1–2 of Python source files are
  now recognized with confidence 0.95 (`249
  <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/249>`_)
- Added ``chardet.universaldetector`` backward-compatibility stub so that
  ``from chardet.universaldetector import UniversalDetector`` works with a
  deprecation warning (`341
  <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/341>`_)

**Fixes:**

- Fixed false UTF-7 detection of ASCII text containing ``++`` or ``+word``
  patterns (`332 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/332>`_)
- Fixed 0.5s startup cost on first ``detect()`` call — model norms are now
  computed during loading instead of lazily iterating 21M entries (`333
  <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/333>`_)
- Fixed undocumented encoding name changes between chardet 5.x and 7.0 —
  ``detect()`` now returns chardet 5.x-compatible names by default (`338
  <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/338>`_)
- Improved ISO-2022-JP family detection — recognizes ESC sequences for
  ISO-2022-JP-2004 (JIS X 0213) and ISO-2022-JP-EXT (JIS X 0201 Kana)
- Fixed silent truncation of corrupt model data (``iter_unpack`` yielded
  fewer tuples instead of raising)
- Fixed incorrect date in LICENSE

**Performance:**

- 5.5x faster first-detect time (~0.42s → ~0.075s) by computing model
  norms as a side-product of ``load_models()``
- ~40% faster model parsing via ``struct.iter_unpack`` for bulk entry
  extraction (eliminates ~305K individual ``unpack`` calls)

**New API parameters:**

- Added ``compat_names`` parameter (default ``True``) to
  :func:`~chardet.detect`, :func:`~chardet.detect_all`, and
  :class:`~chardet.UniversalDetector` — set to ``False`` to get raw Python
  codec names instead of chardet 5.x/6.x compatible display names
- Added ``prefer_superset`` parameter (default ``False``) — remaps legacy
  ISO/subset encodings to their modern Windows/CP superset equivalents
  (e.g., ASCII → Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1 → Windows-1252).
  **This will default to ``True`` in the next major version (8.0).**
- Deprecated ``should_rename_legacy`` in favor of ``prefer_superset`` —
  a deprecation warning is emitted when used

**Improvements:**

- Switched internal canonical encoding names to Python codec names
  (e.g., ``"utf-8"`` instead of ``"UTF-8"``), with ``compat_names``
  controlling the public output format.  See :doc:`usage` for the full
  mapping table.
- Added ``lookup_encoding()`` to ``registry`` for case-insensitive
  resolution of arbitrary encoding name input to canonical names
- Achieved 100% line coverage across all source modules (+31 tests)
- Updated benchmark numbers: 98.2% encoding accuracy, 95.2% language
  accuracy on 2,510 test files
- Pinned test-data cloning to chardet release version tags for
  reproducible builds
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.0.1
   ```
   -------------------

**Fixes:**

- Fixed false UTF-7 detection of SHA-1 git hashes (`324
  <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/324>`_)
- Fixed ``_SINGLE_LANG_MAP`` missing aliases for single-language encoding
  lookup (e.g., ``big5`` → ``big5hkscs``)
- Fixed PyPy ``TypeError`` in UTF-7 codec handling

**Improvements:**

- Retrained bigram models — 24 previously failing test cases now pass
- Updated language equivalences for mutual intelligibility (Slovak/Czech,
  East Slavic + Bulgarian, Malay/Indonesian, Scandinavian languages)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.0.0
   ```
   -------------------

Ground-up, MIT-licensed rewrite of chardet. Same package name, same
public API — drop-in replacement for chardet 5.x/6.x.

**Highlights:**

- **MIT license** (previous versions were LGPL)
- **96.8% accuracy** on 2,179 test files (+2.3pp vs chardet 6.0.0,
  +7.7pp vs charset-normalizer)
- **41x faster** than chardet 6.0.0 with mypyc (**28x** pure Python),
  **7.5x faster** than charset-normalizer
- **Language detection** for every result (90.5% accuracy across 49
  languages)
- **99 encodings** across six eras (MODERN_WEB, LEGACY_ISO, LEGACY_MAC,
  LEGACY_REGIONAL, DOS, MAINFRAME)
- **12-stage detection pipeline** — BOM, UTF-16/32 patterns, escape
  sequences, binary detection, markup charset, ASCII, UTF-8 validation,
  byte validity, CJK gating, structural probing, statistical scoring,
  post-processing
- **Bigram frequency models** trained on CulturaX multilingual corpus
  data for all supported language/encoding pairs
- **Optional mypyc compilation** — 1.49x additional speedup on CPython
- **Thread-safe** ``detect()`` and ``detect_all()`` with no measurable
  overhead; scales on free-threaded Python 3.13t+
- **Negligible import memory** (96 B)
- **Zero runtime dependencies**
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Unified single-byte charset detection with proper language-specific
  bigram models for all single-byte encodings (replaces ``Latin1Prober``
  and ``MacRomanProber`` heuristics)
- 38 new languages: Arabic, Belarusian, Breton, Croatian, Czech, Danish,
  Dutch, English, Esperanto, Estonian, Farsi, Finnish, French, German,
  Icelandic, Indonesian, Irish, Italian, Kazakh, Latvian, Lithuanian,

- EBCDIC detection (CP037, CP500)
- Direct GB18030 support (replaces redundant GB2312 prober)
- Binary file detection
- Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 support
   ```

author: segin
body:
Fixes #xxxx

This pull request updates the documentation in the Z80 regression test suite. The previous comment (`// Bug: NEG with A=0x80 causes overflow`) incorrectly implied that the emulator had a bug when processing `NEG A` where `A=0x80`. 

However, this behavior is a known edge case and hardware quirk of the original Z80 CPU (since `0 - 0x80 = 0x80` which sets the overflow/parity flag). The comment has been updated to explicitly state `// Z80 hardware bug: NEG with A=0x80 causes overflow` to prevent future confusion.

**Changes made:**
- Changed the misleading "Bug:" prefix to "Z80 hardware bug:" in `src/z80/tests_regression.rs`.

author: dacracot
body:
Greptile Summary

This PR (v0.3) restructures the Klondike simulator by reorganising game components into a new `table` package, properly initialising the seven-column board from the deck for the first time, replacing positional CLI arguments with named flags, and introducing a `Global` configuration class. Key changes and findings: - **`table/Board.java`** — The new `Board` correctly deals 28 cards into 7 Klondike columns on construction, but its `playCard()` method is a broken stub that unconditionally returns `true`, which will produce invalid simulation results the moment board-move logic is uncommented in `Klondike.java`. - **`Solitaire.java`** — The new `--attempts` flag parsing crashes with an unhandled `NoSuchElementException` if no integer follows the flag; `cli.hasNextInt()` should guard the `nextInt()` call. - **`Klondike.java`** — The commented-out `board.moveCards()` call references a method that does not exist in `Board`, which would be a compilation error if uncommented. - **`Global.java`** — Introduces public mutable static fields as a global configuration bag; functional for a single-threaded simulator but a design anti-pattern that makes future refactoring harder. - `Goal.java` and `Stack.java` are clean renames/refactors with no logic changes.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Safe to merge for continued development, but contains a crash bug in CLI parsing and a stub that will silently corrupt simulation results when board logic is enabled. - The board-movement path is still commented out so the broken `playCard` stub doesn't affect current runtime behaviour, but the `--attempts` crash is immediately reachable by any user who forgets to supply a number. The global mutable state and missing `moveCards()` method are technical debt risks for future work. - `src/org/dacracot/table/Board.java` (stub `playCard`) and `src/org/dacracot/Solitaire.java` (`--attempts` crash) need attention before this is considered stable.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/org/dacracot/table/Board.java | New Board class replacing the old stub in `play/`; properly initializes 7 Klondike columns from the deck, but `playCard()` is a broken stub that always returns `true` with an unreachable catch block. | | src/org/dacracot/Solitaire.java | CLI argument parsing refactored to named flags (`--one`, `--three`, `--attempts`, `--debug`); contains a crash bug when `--attempts` is provided without a following integer, and the usage message doesn't exit cleanly. | | src/org/dacracot/Global.java | New class holding simulation-wide configuration as public mutable static fields; functional but anti-pattern global mutable state that couples all classes together. | | src/org/dacracot/Klondike.java | Refactored to use `table` package, adds `Board` initialization and a `showAll()` debug helper; board movement logic is still commented out and references a non-existent `moveCards()` method. | | src/org/dacracot/table/Goal.java | Renamed from `play/Goal.java` to `table/Goal.java` with package update and `showGoals()` renamed to `show()` with added section header output; no logic changes. | | src/org/dacracot/table/Stack.java | Renamed from `play/Stack.java` to `table/Stack.java` with package update and `showStacks()` renamed to `show()` with added section header output; no logic changes. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant Solitaire participant Global participant Player participant Klondike participant Deck participant Board participant Goal participant Stack User->>Solitaire: main(args) Solitaire->>Global: cards, tries, debug (set from flags) loop Global.tries times Solitaire->>Player: new Player(Global.cards) Player->>Klondike: new Klondike(flips) Klondike->>Deck: new Deck() Klondike->>Goal: new Goal() Klondike->>Board: new Board(deck) Board->>Deck: getCard(0) × 28 (sevenXseven) Klondike->>Stack: new Stack(deck.getStack(), flips) Player->>Klondike: play() loop until winner or noMoves > 3 Klondike->>Stack: flip() Klondike->>Goal: playCard(upCard) alt card accepted Klondike->>Stack: removeUpCard() else card rejected Klondike->>Stack: flip() end Klondike->>Goal: winner()? end Klondike-->>Player: true/false end Solitaire->>Score: result() Score-->>User: win/loss summary ```

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. `src/org/dacracot/Klondike.java`, line 50-53 ([link](https://github.com/dacracot/klondike3-simulator/blob/2ffbfca9a8e4eaf9cc68718136afa9e06f57f427/src/org/dacracot/Klondike.java#L50-L53)) **`board.moveCards()` referenced in comment does not exist** The commented-out line `// if (board.moveCards()){moves++;}` references a method `moveCards()` that is not defined in `src/org/dacracot/table/Board.java`. If this code is uncommented in a future iteration it will cause a compilation error. Either add the method stub to `Board` or update the comment to reflect the intended API.
Last reviewed commit: 2ffbfca > Greptile also left **4 inline comments** on this PR.

Implement the LSP configuration system (EPIC-4.1) to allow users to customize StringKnife behavior through Zed's `settings.json`. This includes:

- **New `config.rs` module** with typed `Config` struct supporting 6 configuration options:

## Summary

`AuthKitProvider` called `useNavigate()` unconditionally at render time. During SSR with TanStack Start, the Wrap component renders before `RouterProvider` context is established, causing repeated console warnings: *"useRouter must be used inside a `<RouterProvider>` component!"*

This PR removes the `useNavigate` import and hook call entirely. The `handleSignOut` fallback (when no sign-out URL is returned) now uses `window.location.href = returnTo` instead of `navigate({ to: returnTo })`, which is consistent with the primary sign-out path and eliminates the router hook dependency during SSR.

## Manual reproduction steps

1. Check out `main`, install deps, start the example app: `cd example && pnpm dev`
2. Open browser console at `http://localhost:3000` -- observe repeated warnings: *"useRouter must be used inside a `<RouterProvider>` component!"*
3. Check out this branch, restart the example app
4. Open browser console -- observe **0 warnings**

### Before/after evidence

**After (this branch):** Browser console shows 0 warnings related to useRouter/RouterProvider:

![after.png](https://github.com/nicknisi/case-assets/releases/download/assets/after.png)

## What was tested

### Automated
- Full test suite: **175 tests passing** across 16 test files
- Build succeeds with zero TypeScript errors
- `useNavigate` confirmed completely absent from `src/` via grep

### Manual
- Example app started on port 3000
- Home page and client demo page loaded via Playwright
- Browser console shows **0 warnings** (only a 404 for missing favicon)
- The SSR "useRouter must be used inside a RouterProvider" warning is eliminated

author: svozza
body:
## Summary

Add metrics middleware for emitting per-request metrics from the Event Handler HTTP router using the Powertools Metrics utility.

### Changes

- Add `route` field to `RequestContext` populated with the matched route pattern (e.g. `GET /users/:id`), or `null` when no route matches
- Create metrics middleware that emits `latency`, `fault`, and `error` metrics per request
- Use the matched route as a metric dimension (uses `NOT_FOUND` when no route matches to prevent dimension explosion)
- Make `RequestContext` a discriminated union on `responseType`, enabling type-safe access to event-specific properties (e.g. `requestContext.requestId` on API Gateway events but not ALB)
- Add request metadata to metrics:
  - `httpMethod` and `path` for all requests
  - `statusCode` for all requests
  - `ipAddress` from `requestContext.identity.sourceIp` (V1), `requestContext.http.sourceIp` (V2), or `X-Forwarded-For` header (ALB fallback)
  - `userAgent` from request headers
  - `apiGwRequestId` and `apiGwApiId` for API Gateway V1 and V2 events
  - `apiGwExtendedRequestId` for API Gateway V1 events when available
- Remove unused `getResponseType` function (replaced by type guard branching in `#buildRequestContext`)
- Add `@aws-lambda-powertools/metrics` as an optional peer dependency, following the same pattern as the tracer middleware
- Expose the metrics middleware as a subpath export to avoid requiring the metrics dependency
- Unit tests are covered

**Issue number:** closes #4602

author: moomooskycow
body:
Closes #300

## Why This Matters

Cerberus was under-grading meaningful unused runtime dependency findings as `info`, which made them easy to miss and kept them out of warning thresholds. This branch fixes that review-trust gap for issue #300 by promoting strong unused-dependency signals to `minor` during aggregation while keeping the downgrade and reviewer-verdict boundaries intact.

## Trade-offs / Risks

This lane still uses a curated known-large package set plus a narrow finding-text contract, so unknown packages or new phrasing can stay at `info` until a future schema-backed follow-up exists. Reviewer `verdict` fields remain unchanged by design; only finding severity and reviewer stats move, which keeps the change within the issue boundary but limits how much a single promoted finding can influence reviewer-level PASS/WARN/FAIL states.

## Intent Reference

Intent source: [Issue #300](https://github.com/misty-step/cerberus/issues/300)

- Intent: surface meaningful unused runtime dependency findings as actionable review output instead of burying them as `info`.
- Success Conditions: known large runtime dependencies promote to `minor`, cross-reviewer agreement strengthens the signal, and reviewer stats stay aligned after promotion.
- Hard Boundaries: no live bundle-size lookups, no changes to speculative/stale-knowledge downgrades, no promotions above `minor`, no reviewer verdict-field rewrites.
- Non-Goals: broad dead-code severity rewrites outside unused-dependency cases.

## Changes

- Added an aggregation-time promotion pass in `scripts/aggregate-verdict.py` for unused runtime dependency findings.
- Tightened the extraction/guard path so promotion only trusts backtick-quoted package names or explicit `:` / `-` delimiters after the unused-dependency phrase.
- Excluded dev-only dependency findings from both single-reviewer and cross-reviewer promotion paths.
- Updated cross-reviewer annotation to mention only the other agreeing reviewer(s).
- Updated `craft` guidance in `.opencode/agents/maintainability.md` so future reviews classify non-trivial unused runtime dependencies as `minor` by default.
- Added regression coverage for large runtime promotion, dev-only non-promotion, cross-reviewer agreement wording, ambiguous wording non-promotion, and rendered markdown visibility.
- Added `walkthrough/issue-300-reviewer-evidence.md` as the walkthrough artifact for this internal review-semantics change.

## Alternatives Considered

- Do nothing: keeps real dependency hygiene findings buried as `info` and preserves the trust gap.
- Promote in `parse-review.py`: would normalize earlier, but this issue scoped the fix to aggregation and explicitly avoided broader parse-layer changes.
- Expand the finding schema first: better long term, but not available in the current reviewer/parser contract and outside this lane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Given a single reviewer flags an unused dependency with a known non-negligible bundle size (>5kB), when `aggregate-verdict.py` processes the artifact, then that finding is promoted to `minor` and the stats are recomputed accordingly.
- [x] Given 2+ reviewers independently flag the same unused dependency, when `aggregate-verdict.py` aggregates, then the finding is promoted to `minor` and its description records cross-reviewer agreement.
- [x] Given a single reviewer flags an unused dev dependency with trivial size (<5kB), when `aggregate-verdict.py` processes the artifact, then severity remains `info`.
- [x] Given promotion occurs, when `render-findings.py` renders the finding list, then the promoted `minor` finding appears in the rendered markdown output.
- [x] Given the reviewer prompt for `craft` is updated, when a reviewer sees an unused dep in a diff, then it classifies it as `minor` rather than `info` by default.

## Reviewer Evidence

- Start here: [walkthrough/issue-300-reviewer-evidence.md](https://github.com/misty-step/cerberus/blob/codex/issue-300-unused-deps-minor/walkthrough/issue-300-reviewer-evidence.md)
- Fast claim: aggregation now upgrades meaningful unused runtime dependency findings from `info` to `minor`, keeps reviewer stats in sync, and records cross-reviewer agreement without promoting dev-only findings.

## Walkthrough

- Renderer: Diagram-led walkthrough with command evidence
- Artifact: [walkthrough/issue-300-reviewer-evidence.md](https://github.com/misty-step/cerberus/blob/codex/issue-300-unused-deps-minor/walkthrough/issue-300-reviewer-evidence.md)
- Claim: this branch turns meaningful unused runtime dependency findings into actionable review signal without changing reviewer verdict fields.
- Before / After scope: aggregate verdict processing, maintainability reviewer guidance, and regression coverage.
- Persistent verification: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_aggregate_verdict.py -v` and `python3 -m pytest tests/test_render_findings.py -v`
- Residual gap: the known-large dependency list is curated, so unknown packages still require future expansion.

## Manual QA

1. Run `python3 -m pytest tests/test_aggregate_verdict.py -k 'promotes_large_unused_runtime_dependency_to_minor or keeps_large_known_package_as_info_when_dev_dependency or keeps_cross_reviewer_dev_dependencies_as_info or promotes_cross_reviewer_unused_dependency_and_marks_agreement or promoted_finding_renders_in_markdown or ignores_ambiguous_unused_dependency_titles_without_package_name' -v`.
2. Confirm the six issue-specific tests pass and cover promotion, dev-only exclusions, cross-reviewer wording, ambiguous wording, and rendered markdown visibility.
3. Run `python3 -m pytest tests/test_aggregate_verdict.py -v`.
4. Run `python3 -m pytest tests/test_render_findings.py -v`.

## What Changed

Base branch flow:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Reviewer artifact] --> B[Aggregate verdict]
    B --> C[Severity stays as reported]
    C --> D[Stats copied through]
```

This PR flow:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Reviewer artifact] --> B[Aggregate verdict]
    B --> C{Unused runtime dependency signal?}
    C -->|Known large package| D[Promote to minor]
    C -->|Cross-reviewer agreement| D
    C -->|No| E[Leave as info]
    D --> F[Recompute reviewer stats]
    E --> F
```

Architecture/state sketch:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Finding text] --> B[Explicit package extraction]
    B --> C[Known-large runtime package match]
    B --> D[File + package agreement key]
    C --> E[Minor promotion]
    D --> F[Cross-reviewer agreement annotation]
    E --> G[Stat recomputation]
    F --> G
```

The new shape is better because the promotion decision now lives in one aggregation pass that updates both the finding and its stats together, instead of leaving downstream consumers to interpret stale severity counts.

## Before / After

Before: large unused runtime dependencies such as `lodash` could be flagged by one or more reviewers and still remain `info`, which diluted the signal and understated reviewer stats.

After: the same findings promote to `minor` when the signal is strong enough, cross-reviewer agreement is explicit, dev-only findings stay excluded, and stats stay aligned with the promoted severity.

## Test Coverage

- Added issue-specific regression tests in `tests/test_aggregate_verdict.py` for large runtime dependency promotion, dev-only exclusions, cross-reviewer agreement wording, ambiguous wording non-promotion, and rendered markdown visibility.
- Full aggregate and render suites rerun after the rebase and review fixes.
- Gap: the curated package set is intentionally small, so packages outside that set are not yet covered by promotion tests.

## Merge Confidence

High. The strongest evidence is the expanded regression set plus full `tests/test_aggregate_verdict.py` and `tests/test_render_findings.py` reruns after the review fixes. Residual risk is limited to false negatives for large packages not yet in the curated set.

author: santiagomed
body:
## Summary

Previously, binary responses (e.g., `application/octet-stream`, images, audio, video) were processed incorrectly:
- **TypeScript**: `response.text()` corrupts bytes > 127 due to UTF-8 encoding
- **Python**: `response.json()` fails on binary data

## Changes

Now both SDKs detect binary content types and handle them properly:

| SDK | Method | Return Type |
|-----|--------|-------------|
| TypeScript | `response.arrayBuffer()` | `ArrayBuffer` |
| Python | `response.content` | `bytes` |

### Supported Binary Content Types
- `application/octet-stream`
- `image/*`
- `audio/*`
- `video/*`

## Usage

### TypeScript
```typescript
const data = await client.someEndpoint.download({ id: '123' });
const bytes = new Uint8Array(data); // Convert to Uint8Array if needed
```

### Python
```python
data = client.some_endpoint.download(id='123')
# data is already bytes, use directly or save to file
```

body:
**Motivation**

[EIP-8025](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8025) extends the Engine API with endpoints for requesting, delivering, and verifying zkEVM execution proofs, enabling proof-of-proof-of-stake.

**Description**

- 3 new Engine API endpoints: `engine_requestProofsV1`, `engine_verifyExecutionProofV1`, `engine_verifyNewPayloadRequestHeaderV1`
- L1 proof coordinator (`crates/blockchain/proof_coordinator/`) with pull model for prover workers
- Shared prover infrastructure (`crates/prover/`) extracted from `crates/l2/prover/`
- SSZ support via libssz for `NewPayloadRequest` hash tree root computation
- Guest program EIP-8025 mode: takes `(NewPayloadRequest [SSZ], ExecutionWitness [rkyv])`, outputs 33 bytes (32-byte SSZ root + validity boolean)
- `EXECUTION_PROOFS` + `EXECUTION_PROOF_ROOTS` tables with 128-block retention
- Protocol renames for L1/L2 genericity (`BatchRequest` → `InputRequest`, etc.)
- zkevm@v0.3.0 test support (6718 tests passing)
- All code behind `#[cfg(feature = "eip-8025")]`

Docs: [`docs/eip-8025.md`](docs/eip-8025.md)

> **PoC Limitations**
> - No cryptographic proof verification
> - No retry/backoff on callback delivery
> - Pending proof requests are in-memory only
> - ExecBackend generates a 1-byte sentinel proof

**Checklist**

- [ ] Updated `STORE_SCHEMA_VERSION` (crates/storage/lib.rs)

author: jonathankiichikimura
body:
## Path Search Based On:

-  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A*_search_algorithm#Pseudocode

## Useful Links:

- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Uint8Array
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise
- https://fabricjs.com/docs/
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Int32Array
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Float32Array
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiral_optimization_algorithm


## Map Route                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                              
  Adds obstacle-aware walking route suggestions to the favorites floor plan, and a canvas-based wall rectangle editor for admins to define impassable zones.  
                  
  ---                                                                                                                                                         
                  
  ### `db/migrate/20260311155613_add_wall_rects_to_events.rb` _(new)_

  Adds a `wall_rects` JSONB column to `events` for storing admin-defined impassable rectangles in 0–100 coordinate space.

  ---

  ### `app/javascript/controllers/route_viewer_controller.js` _(new)_

  Stimulus controller that renders a suggested walking route as an SVG overlay on the favorites floor plan.

  - **`connect()`** — registers a mousemove handler for the live coordinate readout and hooks into `turbo:before-stream-render` to redraw the route when
  visited state changes.
  - **`disconnect()`** — removes both event listeners registered in `connect()`.
  - **`generate()`** — wired to the "Suggest Route" button. Builds the passability grid on first call then delegates to `_doGenerate()`. Disables the button
  during grid construction.
  - **`toggle()`** — shows or hides the route SVG layer and toggles the button label.
  - **`_buildGrid()`** — constructs a `Uint8Array` passability grid at 300×300. If `wallsValue` is populated, rasterises wall rectangles directly. Otherwise
  loads the floor plan image into a hidden canvas, thresholds pixels (`r+g+b >= 240` = passable), and dilates impassable cells by 1. Wraps `getImageData()` in
   a try/catch for CORS-tainted canvases.
  - **`_getRegion(cx, cy)`** — maps a stop's percentage coordinates to one of three hardcoded venue regions (bottom, top-left, top-right) to prevent the route
   from jumping between physically disconnected areas.
  - **`_initGrid(grid)`** — stores the built grid and pre-allocates all A\* buffers once (`Float32Array` gScore, `Int32Array` cameFrom, parallel typed-array
  heap). Buffers are reused across every A\* call via `.fill()` reset — no per-call allocation.
  - **`_dilate(raw, radius)`** — expands impassable cells outward by `radius` grid cells to create a safety margin around walls and booth outlines.
  - **`_redraw()`** — reads current visited state, recomputes the ordered stop list and path segments, and re-renders the SVG layer.
  - **`_getVisitedBoothSpaces()`** — queries all card elements for checked visited checkboxes and returns their booth space strings as a `Set`.
  - **`_computeRoute(visitedBoothSpaces)`** — nearest-neighbor within priority tiers, grouped by region first so all stops from one area are always
  consecutive with no inter-region interleaving.
  - **`_computePaths(orderedStops)`** — runs A\* for each consecutive same-region stop pair and starts a new segment when the region changes. Falls back to a
  straight line if A\* returns null.
  - **`_astar(sx, sy, ex, ey)`** — 8-directional A\* on the 300×300 grid using the octile-distance heuristic. Inline binary min-heap over typed arrays — zero
  JS objects created during pathfinding.
  - **`_reconstructPath(cameFrom, endIdx, W)`** — walks the `cameFrom` array from end to start to reconstruct the grid-cell path.
  - **`_nearestPassable(x, y)`** — spiral search outward up to radius 20 to find the nearest passable cell to a given grid coordinate.
  - **`_pullString(path)`** — greedy string-pulling: replaces sequences of grid cells with a single straight segment wherever line-of-sight is unobstructed.
  - **`_linePassable(a, b)`** — Bresenham line traversal returning `false` if any cell along the line is impassable. Used by `_pullString`.
  - **`_renderSegments(segments)`** — clears and redraws the SVG route layer: one dashed `<polyline>` per segment (color-coded) and numbered `<circle>` +
  `<text>` waypoint markers at each stop.

  ---

  ### `app/javascript/controllers/map_editor_controller.js`

  - Added `walls: Array` to `static values` to receive existing wall rects from the view.
  - **`save()`** — extended to serialise wall rects (`obj.wallRect === true`) to percentage coordinates and include them as `wall_rects` in the PATCH body.
  - **`renderExistingCoords()`** — extended to render saved wall rects from `wallsValue` as red dashed Fabric rectangles with `rect.wallRect = true`.
  - **`drawWall()`** — enters drag-to-draw mode for a wall rectangle. Same three-handler pattern as `addRect()` but red/dashed style; commits the rect with
  `wallRect = true`. Clicking again while drawing cancels. Rects smaller than 3×3 canvas pixels are discarded as accidental clicks.

  ---

  ### `app/controllers/admin/map_editors_controller.rb`

  - **`update`** — extended to read `wall_rects` from the JSON body and persist it to `event.wall_rects` within the same transaction as coordinate saving.
  Each entry is strong-parameter permitted (`x`, `y`, `w`, `h`) and cast to float.

  ---

  ### `app/controllers/favorites_controller.rb`

  - **`index`** — queries `@map_priorities` (a `booth_space → priority` hash for the current event's favorites) for use by the map and route viewer.

  ---

  ### `app/views/favorites/_map.html.erb`

  Rewrote the partial to mount the `route-viewer` Stimulus controller. Passes booth center coordinates, priority map, floor plan URL, and wall rects as data
  values. Adds "Suggest Route" / "Hide Route" buttons and a coordinate readout element (hover to read x/y in 0–100 space for defining wall rects).

  ---

  ### `app/views/favorites/_favorite_card.html.erb`

  Added `data-booth-space` to each card so `route_viewer_controller` can read visited state per booth space.

  ---

  ### `app/views/shared/_event_map.html.erb`

  Added an opt-in `<g data-route-viewer-target="routeLayer">` SVG group rendered when `show_route_layer: true` is passed as a local. Hidden by default,
  populated by `route_viewer_controller`.

  ---

  ### `app/views/admin/map_editors/show.html.erb`

  - Added `data-map-editor-walls-value` to pass existing wall rects to the Fabric canvas on load.
  - Added a `+ Draw Wall` toolbar button wired to `map-editor#drawWall`.

author: ztanner
body:
In #91158, I wired up the plumbing to indicate whether a partial fallback shell is upgradeable. The previous heuristic was too coarse. This wires up the handling in `next start`. 

This PR teaches the runtime to complete a fallback shell only as far as prerendering allows. Instead of promoting a generic shell like `/[one]/[two]` directly to `/c/foo`, it promotes it to the most specific prerendered shell for that branch, `/c/[two]`, where `[one]` has `generateStaticParams`. That means later requests can reuse the more complete shell, while fully dynamic params continue to stream as dynamic content.

With this change:

- the first request still serves the generic fallback shell immediately
- the background revalidate writes a more specific shell, not a fully concrete route
- later requests for the same prerendered branch reuse that shell
- upgrading stops once only fully dynamic params remain

This keeps the runtime behavior aligned with the build-time `remainingPrerenderableParams` contract from the downstack PR.

author: programcaicai
body:
## Summary
Fixes post-compaction continuation ordering in embedded subscribe lifecycle handling.

When `auto_compaction_end(willRetry=true)` arrives before the retry run actually starts, the old run's `agent_end` was incorrectly consumed as the retry completion signal. This could resolve wait state too early and let the session return before the retry continuation truly resumed/finished.

## Bug scenario
- **Scenario B1 (pre-retry end consumed as retry completion):**
  1. Run emits `auto_compaction_end` with `willRetry=true`.
  2. Original run emits `agent_end` before retry `agent_start`.
  3. Existing logic decrements pending retry immediately on that `agent_end`.
  4. Wait state may resolve before retry actually starts, causing continuation ordering break.

## Why this bug happened
- Retry accounting tracked only "retry expected" count, not "retry has started" count.
- `handleAgentEnd` consumed pending retry on any `agent_end`, including the original run's terminal event.

## Fix approach
- Add `pendingCompactionRetryStarts` counter:
  - increment when retry is noted (`willRetry=true`)
  - decrement when retry `agent_start` is observed
- In lifecycle handling:
  - on `agent_start`, mark retry started when pending-start counter exists
  - on `agent_end`, only resolve retry when started retries exist
  - otherwise keep waiting until retries really start and finish
- Add/adjust regression tests covering delayed retry start and multiple retries ordering.

## Verification
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-pi-session.waits-multiple-compaction-retries-before-resolving.test.ts --reporter=dot`
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-pi-session.splits-long-single-line-fenced-blocks-reopen.test.ts -t "waits for auto-compaction retry to resume before clearing the wait" --reporter=dot`

author: copilot
body:
Full implementation of the CanBankX commercial banking platform per the LOG430 cahier des charges. The initial codebase had no auth, no validation, hardcoded credentials, generic `RuntimeException` error handling, no audit trail, and a single empty test.

## Domain & Use Cases

- **UC-01/02 — Auth & KYC**: JWT stateless auth with BCrypt, `/api/v1/auth/register` and `/login`. KYC workflow: `PENDING → VERIFIED → REJECTED` via dedicated endpoints.
- **UC-03 — Accounts**: `CHECKING`/`SAVINGS` account types with customer existence validation.
- **UC-04 — Consultation**: Balance and transaction history queries.
- **UC-05 — Transfers**: Internal transfers with balance checks, self-transfer prevention.
- **UC-06 — Bill Payments**: `BillPayment` entity, service, and controller with payee tracking.
- **UC-07 — AML Detection**: Flags large transactions (>$10k) and high-frequency patterns (>10/24h) via DB-level count query. Logged to audit trail.
- **Idempotency**: All financial operations accept `Idempotency-Key` header → unique constraint on `Transaction.idempotencyKey` and `BillPayment.idempotencyKey`.
- **Audit**: Append-only `AuditLog` entity recording all mutations across every service.

## API & Error Handling

- All routes versioned under `/api/v1/`
- `@ControllerAdvice` with typed exceptions (`ResourceNotFoundException`, `InsufficientFundsException`, `InvalidAmountException`) → normalized JSON error responses
- `@Valid`/`@NotBlank`/`@Email`/`@Positive` on entities and controller params
- OpenAPI/Swagger via `springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui` with JWT bearer scheme

## Security

- `SecurityConfig`: JWT filter chain, stateless sessions, BCrypt `PasswordEncoder` bean
- CORS restricted to `localhost` by default (configurable via `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`)
- CSRF intentionally disabled (stateless bearer token API — no cookies)
- All credentials externalized: `SPRING_DATASOURCE_*`, `JWT_SECRET`, `GF_ADMIN_*`
- JWT validation logs distinct cases (expired, tampered, malformed)

## Observability & Infrastructure

- **Docker Compose**: PostgreSQL + Customer Service + Prometheus + Grafana + Nginx API Gateway
- **Prometheus**: Scrapes `/actuator/prometheus` at 5s intervals
- **Grafana**: Auto-provisioned datasource + 4 Golden Signals dashboard (latency P95, traffic RPS, error rates, saturation)
- **Nginx**: API gateway with proxy routing, `X-Request-ID` header injection, health endpoint
- **Dockerfile**: Multi-stage build (JDK → JRE), healthcheck

## Testing

28 unit tests with Mockito covering all services:

```
CustomerServiceTest     — 7 tests (create, KYC verify/reject, lookup)
AccountServiceTest      — 6 tests (CHECKING/SAVINGS, invalid type, missing customer)
TransactionServiceTest  — 10 tests (deposit/withdraw/transfer, idempotency, validation)
BillPaymentServiceTest  — 4 tests (pay, idempotency, insufficient funds)
ContextLoads            — 1 test (H2 profile)
```

## CI/CD

GitHub Actions workflow: checkout → JDK 21 → build → test → upload results artifact. Workflow permissions scoped to `contents: read`.

author: pephi27
body:
### Motivation
- Move payroll data persistence from a localStorage-first model to a cloud-first KV model for critical business data to avoid accidental local overwrites and enable cross-device sync.
- Treat a set of payroll keys as authoritative in cloud storage and ensure writes/reads for those keys use cloud writers when available.
- Provide safer migration and restore semantics so critical keys are seeded to cloud only when intended and legacy local caches are cleared after successful hydration.
- Add developer diagnostics to detect/optionally block accidental localStorage use for critical keys during development.

### Description
- Introduces `CRITICAL_PAYROLL_KEYS` and `persistCriticalBusinessKey` / `persistCriticalBusinessKeySoon` to centralize cloud vs local persistence and error handling, and replaces many `localStorage` writes/reads with cloud-aware calls (e.g. replacing JSON fallback reads with empty-object fallbacks and using `persistCriticalBusinessKeySoon(…)`).
- Updates UI saving indicators from "Saved locally" to "Saved to cloud" where appropriate and switches numerous modules (loan tracker, other deductions, DTR save/load, payroll rates, schedules, employees, projects, history) to the new persistence API.
- Enhances the KV sync adapter (`kvSyncAdapter.js`) to treat a set of critical keys as remote-first, add seeding and clearing helpers (`maybeSeedCriticalKeysFromLegacyLocal`, `clearCriticalLegacyLocalCache`), track hydrate state, and avoid exposing legacy local data unless explicit degraded fallback is allowed.
- Changes the backup/restore flow (`backupRestore.js`) so `applyLocalStorage` routes critical keys to cloud writers instead of writing them to localStorage, and adjusts DTR restore to write `att_records_v2` via cloud writer when available.
- Adds a developer diagnostic hook (`installDevLocalStorageDetector`) in `main.js` that can warn or throw when code attempts to access/modify critical keys via `localStorage`/`readKV`/`writeKV` depending on debug/strict flags.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change set.

The toLocaleString() round-trip pattern for timezone conversion loses timezone context when re-parsed by new Date(), causing the server (running in UTC) to calculate the wrong game day during DST transitions. author: nickswalker
body:
Expose xacro_args on the `get_urdf_path` interface. Xacro args define reasonable (and uncountable numbers of) variations of a robot, so it makes sense to allow library users to pass their preferred args in when requesting a URDF. The user can do this currently, but must define their own module or one-off namespace.

```python
# What it takes to pass custom xacro args without this PR
from types import SimpleNamespace

temp_module = SimpleNamespace(
    __name__="robot_descriptions.fr3_without_hand_description",
    REPOSITORY_PATH=fr3_description.REPOSITORY_PATH,
    PACKAGE_PATH=fr3_description.PACKAGE_PATH,
    XACRO_PATH=fr3_description.XACRO_PATH,
    XACRO_ARGS={"hand": "false"},
)

urdf_path = get_urdf_path(temp_module)
```

These uses will be somewhat non-standard definitionally, so it feels okay to not expose xacro args in the higher level loader interface.

Ultimately, I'm interested in being able to easily compose arms and grippers, for which this feature is helpful. I've included a new example script illustrating this, since it might be a common "advanced" use case. Please feel free to remove it

author: copilot
body:
The generated `view.html` had a misleading title and a broken column header when switching to "Group by resolution" mode.

## Changes

- **Rename heading**: `Local Screenshot Viewer` → `Resolution Review`; removed the now-redundant subtitle line and its unused `.subtitle` CSS rule
- **Fix `undefined x undefined` in resolution group headers**: `renderHeader` unconditionally used `column.width + ' x ' + column.height`, but when grouping by resolution the columns are *slides* (no `width`/`height`). Fixed by branching on `groupBy`:

```js
// before — always tried width/height, producing "undefined x undefined" for slides
const detail = state.groupBy === 'slide'
  ? column.width + ' x ' + column.height
  : column.width + ' x ' + column.height;

// after — falls back to the slide key when columns are slides
const detail = state.groupBy === 'slide'
  ? column.width + ' x ' + column.height
  : column.key;
```

body: ## Summary Adds an automated skill quality evaluation pipeline using [promptfoo](https://promptfoo.dev). ### What's included - **`eval/` directory** with 10 pilot skill eval configs - **GitHub Action** (`skill-eval.yml`) — runs evals on PRs that change SKILL.md files - **Generator script** — `python eval/scripts/generate-eval-config.py ` bootstraps eval configs - **Assertion helpers** — reusable JS quality checks - **Documentation** — setup, usage, cost estimates ### Pilot skills (10) | Skill | Domain | Tests | |-------|--------|-------| | copywriting | Marketing | 3 | | cto-advisor | C-Level | 3 | | seo-audit | Marketing | 2 | | content-strategy | Marketing | 2 | | aws-solution-architect | Engineering | 2 | | agile-product-owner | Product | 2 | | senior-frontend | Engineering | 2 | | senior-security | Engineering | 2 | | mcp-server-builder | Engineering | 2 | | launch-strategy | Marketing | 2 | ### How it works 1. PR changes a SKILL.md → Action detects which skills changed 2. Maps changed skills to eval configs (if they exist) 3. Runs `npx promptfoo eval` with LLM-rubric assertions 4. Posts results as PR comment 5. Uploads full results as artifacts ### CI integration - **Non-blocking** — informational only, not a gate (yet) - **Requires** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret - **Cost** — ~$0.05-0.10 per skill eval ($0.50-1.00 for full batch) - **No existing workflows modified** — all new files ### Generate evals for more skills ```bash python eval/scripts/generate-eval-config.py marketing-skill/email-sequence python eval/scripts/generate-eval-config.py engineering-team/devops-engineer ``` ### No existing files modified ✅ ---

### Motivation
- Prevent EF Core from tracking `TaskEntity` instances that are later modified by `TaskExtention.Reset`, which caused the exception `The property 'TaskEntity.Id' is part of a key and so cannot be modified` when saving a task snapshot to storage.

- Add `AsNoTracking()` to `RecursiveTasksCte.Query(context, id, calcId)` in `Persistence/Service/CalculationItems/Storage/StorageCommandService.cs` so the task subtree is loaded detached before `TaskExtention.Reset` mutates clone identities.

body:
## Summary
This PR adds automatic update checking and installation functionality to the application using Tauri's updater plugin. The app now checks for updates on startup and can download and install them with progress tracking.

## Key Changes
- **New updater module** (`src/updater.ts`): Implements `checkForUpdates()` function that checks for available updates, downloads them with progress logging, and relaunches the application
- **Update check on app startup**: Integrated update checking into the App component's initialization lifecycle
- **Tauri configuration**: Added updater plugin configuration to `tauri.conf.json` with GitHub releases endpoint
- **GitHub Actions workflow**: 
  - Added `generate-signing-key.yml` workflow for generating Tauri updater signing keys
  - Updated `release.yml` to sign releases and generate updater metadata with `updaterJsonPreferNsis: true`
- **Plugin integration**: Added `tauri-plugin-updater` and `tauri-plugin-process` dependencies and initialized them in the Tauri backend
- **Capabilities**: Updated default capabilities to include `process:allow-restart` and `updater:default` permissions

## Implementation Details
- The `checkForUpdates()` function accepts an optional `interactive` parameter to control logging behavior
- Download progress is tracked and logged with chunk-based updates
- The update endpoint is configured to fetch `latest.json` from GitHub releases
- Windows installations use passive mode for a seamless update experience
- The public key for signature verification needs to be added to `tauri.conf.json` before deployment

author: abhullar-tt
body:
### Ticket
https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/issues/36891

### What's changed
Quasar DMs can automatically post/ack tile counter credits using interrupts on transaction ids. This pr introduces that support. 
Added new "implicit sync" read/write api on dataflow buffer and dfb_txn_id_descriptor_t to set up transaction ids + isr. These allow caller to issue a noc read into/noc write out of the dfb's backing memory. When a specified threshold (num_entries_to_process_threshold) of reads land into the buffer/writes are sent for a particular transaction id, an ISR fires to post/ack credits to tile counters spanning that region of the dfb. 

Added a global array that tells isr  which tile counters need to be updated (and with how many credits) when a particular txn ID threshold is met.

Currently only use two transaction ids per DFB and only DM0 (capable of fast context switch) services the interrupts for all transactions.  In the future we can play around with distributing this handling per txnID or per DFB across DMs

Note: HW doesn't expose "pending tiles to post" so the dfb class tracks how many credits should have been posted. Details about this issue [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1L2DT0flwW8ENmOc5OvaZoua286Inoq3v8jexCdL6w0s/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.os8orrgqzptp)

- Improves accuracy of total EFC calculations

Track cache token counts we can better estimate the cost of a request and how effective we are caching our input tokens.

body:
This PR updates [chardet](https://pypi.org/project/chardet) from **3.0.4** to **7.1.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.1.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Added PEP 263 encoding declaration detection — `` -*- coding: ... -*-``
  and `` coding=...`` declarations on lines 1–2 of Python source files are
  now recognized with confidence 0.95 (`249
  <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/249>`_)
- Added ``chardet.universaldetector`` backward-compatibility stub so that
  ``from chardet.universaldetector import UniversalDetector`` works with a
  deprecation warning (`341
  <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/341>`_)

**Fixes:**

- Fixed false UTF-7 detection of ASCII text containing ``++`` or ``+word``
  patterns (`332 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/332>`_)
- Fixed 0.5s startup cost on first ``detect()`` call — model norms are now
  computed during loading instead of lazily iterating 21M entries (`333
  <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/333>`_)
- Fixed undocumented encoding name changes between chardet 5.x and 7.0 —
  ``detect()`` now returns chardet 5.x-compatible names by default (`338
  <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/338>`_)
- Improved ISO-2022-JP family detection — recognizes ESC sequences for
  ISO-2022-JP-2004 (JIS X 0213) and ISO-2022-JP-EXT (JIS X 0201 Kana)
- Fixed silent truncation of corrupt model data (``iter_unpack`` yielded
  fewer tuples instead of raising)
- Fixed incorrect date in LICENSE

**Performance:**

- 5.5x faster first-detect time (~0.42s → ~0.075s) by computing model
  norms as a side-product of ``load_models()``
- ~40% faster model parsing via ``struct.iter_unpack`` for bulk entry
  extraction (eliminates ~305K individual ``unpack`` calls)

**New API parameters:**

- Added ``compat_names`` parameter (default ``True``) to
  :func:`~chardet.detect`, :func:`~chardet.detect_all`, and
  :class:`~chardet.UniversalDetector` — set to ``False`` to get raw Python
  codec names instead of chardet 5.x/6.x compatible display names
- Added ``prefer_superset`` parameter (default ``False``) — remaps legacy
  ISO/subset encodings to their modern Windows/CP superset equivalents
  (e.g., ASCII → Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1 → Windows-1252).
  **This will default to ``True`` in the next major version (8.0).**
- Deprecated ``should_rename_legacy`` in favor of ``prefer_superset`` —
  a deprecation warning is emitted when used

**Improvements:**

- Switched internal canonical encoding names to Python codec names
  (e.g., ``"utf-8"`` instead of ``"UTF-8"``), with ``compat_names``
  controlling the public output format.  See :doc:`usage` for the full
  mapping table.
- Added ``lookup_encoding()`` to ``registry`` for case-insensitive
  resolution of arbitrary encoding name input to canonical names
- Achieved 100% line coverage across all source modules (+31 tests)
- Updated benchmark numbers: 98.2% encoding accuracy, 95.2% language
  accuracy on 2,510 test files
- Pinned test-data cloning to chardet release version tags for
  reproducible builds
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.0.1
   ```
   -------------------

**Fixes:**

- Fixed false UTF-7 detection of SHA-1 git hashes (`324
  <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/324>`_)
- Fixed ``_SINGLE_LANG_MAP`` missing aliases for single-language encoding
  lookup (e.g., ``big5`` → ``big5hkscs``)
- Fixed PyPy ``TypeError`` in UTF-7 codec handling

**Improvements:**

- Retrained bigram models — 24 previously failing test cases now pass
- Updated language equivalences for mutual intelligibility (Slovak/Czech,
  East Slavic + Bulgarian, Malay/Indonesian, Scandinavian languages)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.0.0
   ```
   -------------------

Ground-up, MIT-licensed rewrite of chardet. Same package name, same
public API — drop-in replacement for chardet 5.x/6.x.

**Highlights:**

- **MIT license** (previous versions were LGPL)
- **96.8% accuracy** on 2,179 test files (+2.3pp vs chardet 6.0.0,
  +7.7pp vs charset-normalizer)
- **41x faster** than chardet 6.0.0 with mypyc (**28x** pure Python),
  **7.5x faster** than charset-normalizer
- **Language detection** for every result (90.5% accuracy across 49
  languages)
- **99 encodings** across six eras (MODERN_WEB, LEGACY_ISO, LEGACY_MAC,
  LEGACY_REGIONAL, DOS, MAINFRAME)
- **12-stage detection pipeline** — BOM, UTF-16/32 patterns, escape
  sequences, binary detection, markup charset, ASCII, UTF-8 validation,
  byte validity, CJK gating, structural probing, statistical scoring,
  post-processing
- **Bigram frequency models** trained on CulturaX multilingual corpus
  data for all supported language/encoding pairs
- **Optional mypyc compilation** — 1.49x additional speedup on CPython
- **Thread-safe** ``detect()`` and ``detect_all()`` with no measurable
  overhead; scales on free-threaded Python 3.13t+
- **Negligible import memory** (96 B)
- **Zero runtime dependencies**
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Unified single-byte charset detection with proper language-specific
  bigram models for all single-byte encodings (replaces ``Latin1Prober``
  and ``MacRomanProber`` heuristics)
- 38 new languages: Arabic, Belarusian, Breton, Croatian, Czech, Danish,
  Dutch, English, Esperanto, Estonian, Farsi, Finnish, French, German,
  Icelandic, Indonesian, Irish, Italian, Kazakh, Latvian, Lithuanian,
  Macedonian, Malay, Maltese, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian,
  Scottish Gaelic, Serbian, Slovak, Slovene, Spanish, Swedish, Tajik,
  Ukrainian, Vietnamese, Welsh
- ``EncodingEra`` filtering via new ``encoding_era`` parameter
- ``max_bytes`` and ``chunk_size`` parameters for ``detect()``,
  ``detect_all()``, and ``UniversalDetector``
- ``-e``/``--encoding-era`` CLI flag
- EBCDIC detection (CP037, CP500)
- Direct GB18030 support (replaces redundant GB2312 prober)
- Binary file detection
- Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 support

**Breaking changes:**

- Dropped Python 3.7, 3.8, and 3.9 (requires Python 3.10+)
- Removed ``Latin1Prober`` and ``MacRomanProber``
- Removed EUC-TW support
- Removed ``LanguageFilter.NONE``
- ``detect()`` default changed to ``encoding_era=EncodingEra.MODERN_WEB``

**Fixes:**

- Fixed CP949 state machine
- Fixed SJIS distribution analysis (second-byte range >= 0x80)
- Fixed UTF-16/32 detection for non-ASCII-heavy text
- Fixed GB18030 ``char_len_table``
- Fixed UTF-8 state machine
- Fixed ``detect_all()`` returning inactive probers
- Fixed early cutoff bug
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.2.0
   ```
   -------------------

- Added support for running the CLI via ``python -m chardet``
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.1.0
   ```
   -------------------

- Added ``should_rename_legacy`` argument to remap legacy encoding names
  to modern equivalents
- Added MacRoman encoding prober
- Added ``--minimal`` flag to ``chardetect`` CLI
- Added type annotations and mypy CI
- Added support for Python 3.11
- Removed support for Python 3.6
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.0.0
   ```
   -------------------

- Added Johab Korean prober
- Added UTF-16/32 BE/LE probers
- Added test data for Croatian, Czech, Hungarian, Polish, Slovak,
  Slovene, Greek, Turkish
- Improved XML tag filtering
- Made ``detect_all`` return child prober confidences
- Dropped Python 2.7, 3.4, 3.5 (requires Python 3.6+)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.0.0
   ```
   -------------------

- Added ``detect_all()`` function returning all candidate encodings
- Converted single-byte charset probers to nested dicts (performance)
- ``CharsetGroupProber`` now short-circuits on definite matches
  (performance)
- Added ``language`` field to ``detect_all`` output
- Dropped Python 2.6, 3.4, 3.5
   ```
   
  
</details>

author: musa-dabwe
body:
This change implements a "Smart Sequential Suggestion Algorithm" for the T9 keyboard. It ensures that the primary suggestion (Slot 1) always matches the exact number of keys tapped by the user. Subsequent slots are filled with other exact matches or the shortest probable completions, sorted by frequency. 

Key changes include:
- Bucketing suggestions into exact-length and longer matches in both XT9 and Multi-tap modes.
- Sorting longer completions by length (ascending) first to provide a natural word-growth experience.
- Enabling prefix completions from the very first key tap.
- Treating the raw digit sequence as a last-resort fallback, hidden when any dictionary matches are available.
- Leveraging the learned dictionary's frequency boost to prioritize user-specific words.

body: # The following checklist is mandatory. Your PR will be closed if you remove the checklist or do not answer the questions to a satisfactory level. Use of LLM is **strictly forbidden** for any part of this checklist (even for improving language). ### Your checklist for this pull request - [x] Have you followed all the steps from our [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/pgmpy/pgmpy/blob/dev/Contributing.md)? - [x] Does the PR fully address the linked issue and is within its defined scope? If you are still working on the PR, mark it as draft. - [x] Are all the GitHub Actions checks passing? If not, mark your PR as draft while you fix it. Please answer the following questions: - Did you use an LLM for any assistance? Please describe how and what you used it for? LLM was used to understanding the existing code base of pgmpy. I also used LLM to translate the official DAGMA (https://github.com/kevinsbello/dagma) into sklearn compatible to make it fit into pgmpy architecture. The main use of LLM for coding was done inside the `_objective` method to implement the helper functions _score, _h and _func from official source code to `DAGMA.py` file under `pgmpy/causal_dicovery`. I also used it to figure out the mathematical masking approach for incorporating `ExpertKnowledge` - Are you able to fully explain your changes? We expect you to fully understand the algorithm and take full responsibility for any changes in this PR. Yes, I fully understand the implemented algorithm using the DAGMA paper and the source code as reference. I transitioned the DAGMA's core logic into `_fit` method. I understand how the `L1 penalty` ensures sparsity, how the `Least Squares loss` ensures data fidelity, and how the M-matrix `log-determinant` constraint penalizes cycles and how the central path philosophy of DAGMA works by managing the central path parameter `mu` through a decay loop. I am fully responsible for how the math bridges with the `BaseCausalDiscovery` class - What steps have you taken to verify that the changes correctly address the issue? And what edge cases have you considered? I built a dedicated pytest suite for DagmaLinear model using ideas from test_GES.py as a blueprint(`TestGESCore` -> `TestDagmaLinearCore` etc ), data generation via pytest fixtures, expert knowledge testing under `TestGESExpertKnowledge` class. For edge cases, I specifically handled the scenario where a dataset might have only 1 feature (raising a ValueError), and I explicitly verified that setting the optimization bounds to (0, 0) on the diagonal which perfectly prevents self-loops for DAG. - Has the LLM added try-except blocks? They will need to be removed; any error handling must be explicit. No - Have you used LLM for generating tests? They need to be compressed into a smaller number of tests without reducing coverage. A LLM was used to help structure the tests, but they were strictly modeled after the existing `test_GES.py` file rather than being blindly generated. The tests are already heavily compressed to avoid bloat: instead of writing dozens of manual edge-case tests, I used sklearn.utils.estimator_checks.parametrize_with_checks to run the entire sklearn compliance battery in a single function. The mathematical assertions are condensed into just two minimal classes using a single shared pytest fixture: one testing core edge recovery and bounding, and one testing expert knowledge masking. ### Issue number(s) that this pull request fixes - Fixes #2513 ### List of changes to the codebase in this pull request - PR for the introducing the `DAGMA` algorithm into pgmpy as part of my GSoC/ESoC 2026 project. The algorithm is implemented under `pgmpy/causal_discovery` ### **Proposed API Design & Integration:** - This PR proposes to include DAGMA continuous optimization Algorithm. The algorithm will be integrated under `pgmpy/causal_discovery/` as `DAGMA.py`. - It will contain two classes namely DagmaLinear and DagmaNonLinear. - DAGMA introduces a novel acyclicity charecterization based on Log-Determinant Constrain (`h(W)=−logdet(sI−W∘W)+dlogs`) under the domain of the set of M-matrices to acyclicity and structure learning for DAGs. - Optimization Loop of DAGMA: Approach based on the central path optimization method guaranteed to return a `DAG` at convergence. It pivots away from from the commonly adopted augmented Lagrangian scheme. ### Key Advantages 1. **Log-Determinant Constrain (`h(W)=−logdet(sI−W∘W)+dlogs`)** The log-det regularizer is preferred over existing acyclicity regularizers due to - It does not diminish cycles of any length [Argument (i) of paper] - Has better behaved gradients [Argument (ii) of paper] - Computing is fastser - roughly 10x [Argument (iii) of paper] 2. **It is versatile as it** - Supports linear and nonlinear causal relationships - Handles generalized linear models via logistic scoring - Works with continuous and binary data ### References: - **PAPER:** Title: "DAGMA: Learning DAGs via M-matrices and a Log-Determinant Acyclicity Characterization" Authors: Kevin Bello, Bryon Aragam, Pradeep Ravikumar URL: https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2022/file/36e2967f87c3362e37cf988781a887ad-Paper-Conference.pdf - **IMPLEMENTATION:** Official Repository: https://github.com/kevinsbello/dagma Documentation: https://dagma.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ License: MIT (compatible with pgmpy) ### Possible API design (DagmaLinear) cc: @ankurankan, @DARHWOLF

body:
## Summary

### Printer fixes (`src/ir/transforms/python_printer.cpp`)
- Change `TileView`/`TensorView` output from keyword subscript syntax to positional call syntax — keyword subscripts (`Tile[..., tile_view=...]`) are invalid Python syntax on 3.10/3.11 (PEP 637 requires 3.12+)
- Always emit `stride` + `layout` when `TensorView` is non-trivial; emit `pl.TensorView()` even for all-default fields to preserve structural presence in print-parse roundtrip
- Extend `CollectDynVarNames` to scan `TensorView.valid_shape`/`stride` and all function body statements so `pl.dynamic()` declarations are always emitted in the printed program header
- Add `BuildVarRenameMap` to deduplicate SSA-shadowed `Var` names in DFS pre-order (e.g. two `Var`s both named `i` → `i` and `i_1`)
- Normalize `tensor.add` with scalar RHS to `tensor.adds` to match Python API dispatch
- Print `tile.full` with `dtype=`/`value=` keyword args to avoid ambiguity between dtype enum and positional expression
- Always print `tile.load` in full 5-arg form to prevent default-filling mismatch on re-parse
- Use yield expression type for LHS annotation in `PrintYieldAssignmentVars` instead of `return_var` type

### Parser fixes (`python/pypto/language/parser/`)
- `type_resolver.py`: add `_is_tileview_node`, `_is_tensorview_node`, `_resolve_tileview`, `_resolve_tensorview` helpers to parse the new positional-call `TileView`/`TensorView` format; support `[shape, dtype, memref, tileview]` subscript form for roundtrip
- `text_parser.py`: add `_AutoDynVar` dict subclass to exec namespace so body-level dyn vars auto-created on re-parse prevent `NameError`
- `ast_parser.py`: infer loop-var dtype from range bounds to preserve roundtrip fidelity; allow chunk loops to carry `init_values` (remove incorrect validation); defer `return_var` registration until after body parse to use actual yield LHS names; fold constant negation (`-ConstInt`/`-ConstFloat`) for roundtrip stability; handle bare `pl.yield_()` as `EvalStmt` without creating duplicate `YieldStmt`; parse `MemorySpace` enum attrs as `ConstInt`

## Testing
- [x] Added `TestTileViewTensorViewPrinting`: verify no keyword subscript in output, printed type is valid Python syntax, `TensorView` always emitted, and type_resolver can re-parse the new format
- [x] Added `TestDynVarAndSSARename`: verify dyn var header declaration and SSA-shadowed vars get unique printed names
- [x] Added `TestOpOutputNormalization`: verify `tensor.add` with scalar RHS prints as `tensor.adds`, and `tile.full` emits `dtype=` keyword
- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (clang-format, ruff, pyright)

Closes #323

author: ivchenkoil
body:
## Summary
This PR completely replaces the tickets management system with a new catalog application for a security equipment company called "СпецМонтаж". The application now serves as a product catalog and service showcase website instead of an internal ticket tracking system.

## Key Changes

### Application Structure
- **Removed**: `tickets` app (models, views, forms, templates, tests, migrations, fixtures)
- **Added**: `catalog` app with models for equipment categories and contact requests

### Models
- **New Category model**: Stores equipment categories (СКУД, видеонаблюдение, охранные системы, etc.) with slug, description, icon, and ordering
- **New ContactRequest model**: Captures customer inquiries with name, email, phone, and message fields
- **Removed**: Ticket and Comment models

### Views & URLs
- **New views**: 
  - `index()` - Homepage with featured categories
  - `equipment_list()` - Full equipment catalog
  - `equipment_detail()` - Category detail pages
  - `services()` - Services overview page
  - `contacts()` - Contact form with success redirect
- **New URL patterns**: Catalog-focused routes replacing ticket management routes

### Templates
- **New pages**: 
  - `index.html` - Homepage with hero section and category showcase
  - `equipment_list.html` - Catalog grid view
  - `equipment_detail.html` - Category details with breadcrumbs
  - `services.html` - Service offerings (design, installation, maintenance)
  - `contacts.html` - Contact form with company info
  - `contact_success.html` - Confirmation page
- **Updated base.html**: New navigation menu, Bootstrap Icons integration, custom styling
- **Removed**: All ticket-related templates

### Styling & Assets
- **Added**: `static/css/style.css` with custom styling for hero sections, card hover effects, icon circles, and responsive design
- **Added**: Bootstrap Icons CDN integration
- **Updated**: Base template with improved navbar and footer

### Fixtures & Data
- **Added**: `categories.json` with 5 pre-configured equipment categories (СКУД, видеонаблюдение, охранные системы, системы оповещения, системы пожаротушения)
- **Removed**: Sample ticket fixtures

### Testing
- **New**: `catalog/tests/test_views.py` with tests for all catalog views
- **Removed**: `tickets/tests/test_views.py`

### Configuration
- Updated `settings.py`: Replaced `tickets` with `catalog` app, added static files configuration
- Updated `urls.py`: Replaced ticket routes with catalog routes
- Updated `.gitignore`: Added staticfiles directory

## Implementation Details
- Uses slug-based URLs for equipment categories instead of numeric IDs
- Contact form uses Django ModelForm for automatic validation and database persistence
- Responsive Bootstrap 5 layout with custom CSS enhancements
- Fixture-based category data for easy deployment and testing

### Motivation

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a CHECK-ONLY verification hook that makes the app behave as PRO from startup (for testing) without post-hoc UI-only hacks. 
- Prevent bulk export/preview races that cause blob/file invalidation errors by isolating UI refresh steps that can interfere with export I/O while preserving the normal successful export flow. 

### Description
- Added a check-only forced-PRO hook in `renderer/prototype.html` (`CHECK_ONLY_FORCE_PRO_TIER`, `getCheckOnlyForcedTier()`, `applyCheckOnlyForcedTier()`), and applied it to the final shared tier decision paths used by guards and UI (`getStandardOfflineGatingTier`, `setCache`, `buildState`, `_refreshState`) so guard and UI reference the same forced tier and a one-time log `[CHECK ONLY] FORCE PRO ENABLED` is emitted at startup. 
- Kept existing export success structure intact: `runJob` still calls `await setActiveFile(id, {force:true})` and `buildExportWavBytes` still relies on `state.buffer / state.srcFmtPayload / state.srcDataPayload` and may call `setActiveFile` as before. 
- Introduced minimal bulk-run isolation to reduce blob/file invalidation races by adding `state._bulkJobRunning = true/false` around `runJob` bulk loop and suppressing costly `requestFullRefresh(...)` calls inside `setActiveFile` (only while `_bulkJobRunning` is true). 
- Changes limited to a single file: `renderer/prototype.html` (no changes to `main.js`); PR is explicitly CHECK ONLY / NOT FOR MERGE.

### Testing
- Ran targeted code searches (`rg`) to locate tier/guard/export/state code paths and confirmed hook placement and preserved export preconditions; this completed successfully. 
- Verified the modified file with `git diff --check` and committed the change locally; there were no whitespace or syntax problems from the diff check. 
- Confirmed the commit and that only `renderer/prototype.html` was modified; commit succeeded. 
- Note: attempted to create a branch from `origin/main` but `origin` remote is not configured in this environment, so no remote rebase/CI runs were possible here.

author: mergify[bot]
body:
These are the same changes from https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/pull/11155, but with rekey of the `enable-bls12-381-syscall`.

#### Problem

The sol_curve_validate_point syscall expects strictly uncompressed BLS12-381 points, but the underlying blst library auto-detects formats based on flag bits. This introduces a representation malleability vulnerability:

- If the compression flag (0x80) is set on a 96-byte G1 or 192-byte G2 input, blst treats it as a compressed point and reads only the first half of the buffer.
- The trailing bytes are completely ignored, allowing an attacker to append arbitrary garbage data to the second half of a valid compressed point.
- As a result, numerous distinct byte arrays can successfully validate and decode as the exact same logical curve point.
- Additionally, the sort/parity flag (0x20) must be explicitly rejected for uncompressed points to prevent a similar 1-bit malleability vector.

#### Summary of Changes

Added a strict 0xa0 bitmask check prior to uncompressed point deserialization for both PodG1Point and PodG2Point to explicitly reject the compression (0x80) and sort (0x20) flags. This enforces the correct uncompressed format and eliminates representation malleability while safely preserving the infinity flag (0x40) needed for valid points at infinity.<hr>This is an automatic backport of pull request #11235 done by [Mergify](https://mergify.com).

## Changes

### Two-level command parsing (IMPORTANT)
`AddressBookParser` reads the first word only, but our commands use two words (`alias add`, `alias delete`). 
Rather than reworking the parser, we split it into two levels:

alias add n/Benjamin al/Benjumpin
│           │
│           └─ AliasCommandParser routes "add" → AddAliasCommandParser
│
└─ AddressBookParser routes "alias" → AliasCommandParser


To add `contact` or `game` commands later, just create a new entity parser and add one `case` in `AddressBookParser`.

### New files
- `AliasCommandParser` — routes `add`/`delete` to sub-parsers

author: dongzhuoranzhou
body:
httpx.AsyncClient defaults to trust_env=True, which reads http_proxy/ https_proxy from the environment and routes requests through the proxy. On clusters where proxy env vars are set for external internet access (e.g. W&B logging), all intra-cluster SGLang HTTP calls (/generate, /update_weights_from_distributed, /health, etc.) are routed through the proxy, resulting in 503 Service Unavailable errors.

The standard workaround of adding 10.0.0.0/8 to no_proxy does not work for httpx — unlike requests, httpx does not support CIDR notation in no_proxy (only exact hostnames/IPs and the * wildcard are supported).

Set trust_env=False on both AsyncClient instances in http_utils.py:
- local client in init_http_client()
- Ray actor client in _init_ray_distributed_post()

These clients are exclusively used for intra-cluster SGLang communication and should never be routed through a system proxy.
