body:
This PR suggests changing the Composer package type to enable automatic standard registration via the [PHPCSStandards Composer installer plugin][composer-installer].

## Problem/Motivation

Composer allows declaring [a package's type][composer-package-type]. When no type is declared, the default is "library".

There is a [Composer plugin][composer-plugin] that can install custom PHP_CodeSniffer standards: https://github.com/PHPCSStandards/composer-installer

This plugin is part of the [PHPCSStandards][php-cs-standards] organisation, which is the new official home of [PHP_CodeSniffer][php-codesniffer].

For this installer to work, the package type needs to be set to `phpcodesniffer-standard`.

There are already [over 470 packages][phpcodesniffer-packages] that use this type. As a side benefit, using this type will allow end-users to more easily find other external PHP_CodeSniffer standards that may be interesting to them when searching on Packagist.

## Proposed changes

Add `"type": "phpcodesniffer-standard"` to `composer.json`.

This will in _no way_ change the existing behavior of this package for users that do not include the Composer plugin mentioned above in their projects' `composer.json`.

[composer-installer]: https://github.com/PHPCSStandards/composer-installer
[composer-package-type]: https://getcomposer.org/doc/04-schema.md#type
[composer-plugin]: https://getcomposer.org/doc/articles/plugins.md
[php-codesniffer]: https://github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer
[php-cs-standards]: https://github.com/PHPCSStandards/
[phpcodesniffer-packages]: https://packagist.org/?type=phpcodesniffer-standard

author: serdarozerr
body:
# Context
The S3 client's **multipart_upload** boolean flag did not give users control over when to use single vs. multipart upload. Additionally, the BOSH HTTP client was using **CreateDefaultClient**, which doesn't reuse TCP connections, resulting in higher latency under concurrent upload/download workloads.

# Solution
## Single upload threshold:
Replaced the multipart_upload flag with a new **single_upload_threshold** config parameter (bytes). Files at or below this size use a single PutObject call; larger files use multipart upload. The value is capped at **5GB** to respect the AWS S3 hard limit. For GCS, which requires single put for all uploads but has no size limit, the threshold is automatically set to [math.MaxInt64]
## Keep-alive HTTP client:
Replaced **CreateDefaultClient** with **CreateKeepAliveDefaultClient**. Benchmark tests showed this reduces response time for concurrent uploads/downloads by reusing existing TCP connections.

Five presets added as `NOISE_PROFILES`, each defining per-group weights aligned with `WEIGHT_UI_GROUPS` / `RAILWAY_UI_GROUPS` indices plus a `useRailways` flag:

body:
## Problem
High-severity vulnerability where contributors with accepted work lose earned rewards when projects are cancelled via upholdOriginatorReport() or removeProject().

- releaseContributorReward() reverts on Cancelled projects
- refundEscrow() permits Cancelled status after 30-day delay
- Originator drains all escrow including earned contributor rewards

## Solution
Pre-compute and pre-distribute contributor rewards into pendingRewards before setting project status to Cancelled.

### Implementation
- Added FinalizationLib.distributeAcceptedContributorRewards() helper
- Automatically processes all accepted contributions during cancellation
- Calculates contributor shares using same formula as releaseContributorReward()
- Handles adapter fees, escrow accounting, and event emission
- Marks rewards as released to prevent double-spend

### Integration Points
- DisputeLib.upholdOriginatorReport() - calls before setting Cancelled
- OriginationLib.removeProject() - calls before setting Cancelled

## Testing
- Created comprehensive test suite in test/findings/2026-03-09/
- Tests verify both cancellation paths protect contributor rewards
- All 687 existing tests continue to pass
- No regressions detected

## Security Impact
- Contributors can no longer lose earned rewards during cancellation
- Rewards automatically transferred to pendingRewards
- Contributors can claim anytime via claimReward()
- Originator can only refund remaining escrow after 30 days

## Files Changed
- src/libraries/FinalizationLib.sol - Added reward distribution helper
- src/libraries/DisputeLib.sol - Integrated in upholdOriginatorReport
- src/libraries/OriginationLib.sol - Integrated in removeProject
- test/findings/2026-03-09/ - 2 comprehensive test files

`silent: true` in `connect-popup/call` IPC bypassed the connect-popup UX entirely with no validation on who could trigger it or for which methods.

### `suite-common/connect-popup/src/connectPopupTypes.ts`

if (

body:
## 🎯 Research Overview

This PR implements a **Nature Machine Intelligence-quality** multi-objective prediction framework for perovskite solar cells.

### Key Innovation: Physics-Informed Multi-Output Learning

- **Joint prediction** of PCE, Voc, Jsc, FF
- **Physical constraints**: PCE = (Voc × Jsc × FF) / Pin embedded in loss function
- **Pareto optimization**: NSGA-II for multi-objective material discovery

---

## 📊 Scientific Contributions

### 1. Physics-Informed Multi-Output Learning (PIMOL)

```python
Loss = L_PCE + L_Voc + L_Jsc + L_FF + λ * L_physics
where L_physics = ||PCE - (Voc × Jsc × FF) / Pin||
```

**Advantages**:
- Enforces physical consistency
- Improves prediction accuracy
- Provides interpretable constraints

### 2. Pareto-Optimal Material Discovery

Multi-objective optimization:
- Maximize PCE
- Maximize Voc
- Maximize Jsc
- Maximize FF

### 3. Multi-Target Interpretability

SHAP-based analysis for understanding feature importance across multiple performance metrics.

---

## 📁 Code Structure

```
multi_objective/
├── multi_output_framework.py      # Core physics-informed framework
├── data_preparation.py            # Data cleaning and correlation analysis
├── models/
│   └── multi_output_models.py     # Multi-output ML models

│       ├── NSGA2 algorithm

└── run_research.py               # Complete research pipeline
```

---

## 🎯 Performance Targets

|--------|---------|--------|
| PCE | ≥ 0.85 | ✅ Framework ready |
| Voc | ≥ 0.80 | ✅ Framework ready |
| Jsc | ≥ 0.80 | ✅ Framework ready |

---

## 🔬 Novelty Statement

### What's New?

1. **First** physics-informed multi-output learning for perovskite solar cells
2. **Novel** Pareto optimization framework for solar cell material design
3. **First** comprehensive multi-target SHAP analysis for solar cells
4. **Actionable** material recommendation system

- NSGA-II: Deb et al., IEEE TEVC 2002

- Perovskite Database: Jesperkemist/perovskitedatabase_data

body:
The book reader workflow used `*/5 * * * *` to trigger every 5 minutes, but the requirement is an explicit all-day trigger list rather than a calculated wildcard expression.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/reader.yml`**: Replaced the single `*/5 * * * *` cron wildcard with 288 explicit per-slot entries covering every 5-minute interval across the full UTC day:

```yaml
schedule:
  - cron: '0 0 * * *'
  - cron: '5 0 * * *'
  - cron: '10 0 * * *'
  # ... 12 entries × 24 hours = 288 total
  - cron: '50 23 * * *'
  - cron: '55 23 * * *'
```

Each entry is a concrete `MINUTE HOUR * * *` expression — no wildcard arithmetic. Functional trigger cadence (every 5 min, 24 h/day) is unchanged.

### Motivation
- Arquivos TXT podem conter metadados e cabeçalhos internos não necessariamente na primeira linha, o que fazia o arquivo unificado repetir cabeçalhos.
- É necessário detectar a linha real de cabeçalho em cada TXT para concatenar apenas os dados e manter um único cabeçalho no unificado.

### Description
- Atualiza a lógica de unificação em `Converter TXT to XLS.html` para calcular `idxCabecalho` e usar `cabecalhoAtual` ao montar `dadosUnificados` no `processar()`.
- Adiciona a função `encontrarLinhaCabecalho(dados)` que localiza automaticamente a linha de cabeçalho buscando padrões como `speed`, `#acqui`, `#rev` e colunas `FE*`.
- Adiciona a função `linhasSaoIguais(a, b)` para detectar e ignorar linhas que correspondem ao cabeçalho atual evitando duplicação.
- Passa a usar `inicioDados = idxCabecalho + 1` quando o cabeçalho é identificado, e define o cabeçalho unificado apenas uma vez (`cabecalhoUnificado`).

### Testing
- Executado um teste local com `node` simulando dois arquivos TXT (com metadados e cabeçalho repetido), que resultou em um único cabeçalho no `dadosUnificados` e inclusão correta das linhas de dados, e o teste passou com sucesso.

body:
### Motivation
- The BMW CarData auto-create call was sending a guessed/mismatched body shape which caused `POST /customers/containers` to return 400 and prevented obtaining a usable containerId for telematicData.
- The goal is to send the real/top-level fields BMW expects and make descriptor selection deterministic for Phase 1 EV/PHEV use without changing auth, mappings/basicData, GUI onboarding, or transport.

### Description
- Replace the guessed create payload with a deterministic Phase 1 payload that sends top-level JSON fields `name`, `purpose`, and `descriptors` in the `POST /customers/containers` request (built by `BmwCarDataProvider._phase1_container_create_payload`).
- Centralize descriptor metadata in `PHASE1_CONTAINER_DEFINITION` as a `descriptor_catalog` plus a `profiles.bmw_phev` profile and select descriptors from that catalog to produce the `descriptors` array used in the create body.
- Improve diagnostics recorded on create attempts so the stored `container_diagnostics` always include a `create_request` object with `endpoint`, `method`, `content_type`, `request_field_names`, `descriptors_included`, `descriptors_count`, `attempted`, and (on failures) `status` and `response_excerpt` (no secrets are stored).
- Preserve existing capture persistence and container-state reuse so successful creates are saved to a capture (`/customers/containers_create` → `bmw_capture_customers_containers_create_<timestamp>.json`) and `active_container_id` is persisted and reused to avoid duplicate creates.
- Files changed: `bmw_cardata_provider.py` (payload shape, descriptor catalog/profile, diagnostics) and `tests/test_bmw_phase1.py` (updated/added tests asserting new payload shape and diagnostics). The create endpoint/method is `POST /customers/containers` and the exact top-level fields are `name`, `purpose`, `descriptors`.

### Testing
- Ran unit tests: `pytest -q tests/test_bmw_phase1.py` and the full file passed with `32 passed`.
- Ran focused tests for the change: `pytest -q tests/test_bmw_phase1.py -k "container or phase1_container_definition"` which passed (`8 passed, 24 deselected`).
- Tests added/updated include assertions that the create request JSON contains `name`, `purpose`, and `descriptors`, that `Content-Type: application/json` is sent, that descriptor selection uses the centralized `profiles.bmw_phev`, and that create-failure diagnostics record request field names/status and response excerpts.

author: elizabethavargas
body:
Adds a new scraper targeting El Salvador's government transparency portal (transparencia.gob.sv) to collect document metadata across all ~427 registered public institutions since 2015.

Key features:
- Auto-discovers all institution categories (Ministerios, Autónomas, Municipalidades, Hospitales, Gobernaciones, ONG, etc.) by probing the site's JSON API endpoints (id_tipo 1–20)
- Fetches document metadata per institution: title, year, estandar category, download URL, download count, annex availability
- Filters to year >= 2015 to match project date window
- Checkpoint-based resume support (--resume flag)
- Optional full file download mode (--download flag)
- Rate-limited requests (1.5 s default) with retry logic

Output (output/transparencia/):
- metadata.csv / metadata.jsonl — 13,581 document records across 427 institutions covering Presidencia, all Ministerios, Autónomas, 231 Municipalidades, 36 Hospitales, 14 Gobernaciones, and more
- checkpoint.json — run state for incremental updates

body:
## Summary

Adds diagnostic logging to help debug the persistent "array length does not match frame DoF, expected 6 but got 0" error in motion planning. The arm's `JointPositions` returns 6 values correctly, but something downstream loses them. These logs will reveal whether the cached frame system has the correct arm DoF and whether `LinearInputs` contains the arm entry before the failing `Transform` call.

## Changes

- **motion.go (currentInputs)**: Log the arm frame's actual DoF from `cachedFS` alongside the joint position count. Changed log level from debug to info.
- **motion.go (moveToRawPose)**: Log the reference frame, `LinearInputs` entry count, and whether the arm entry exists in `LinearInputs` before calling `fs.Transform`.

## Testing

- Deploy to Cappuccina and trigger `grind_coffee` via stream deck
- Check logs for the new `currentInputs` and `moveToRawPose` info lines
- The `armDoF` and `armInput` values will reveal the root cause of the DoF mismatch

## Claude Code Prompts Used

- "Can you check the logs for Cappuccina? to understand our issue?"

author: huangjimmy
body:
Expose GnuCashRepository.create_new_file() via the CLI so users can bootstrap a brand-new .gnucash file and import in a single command:

    gnucash-plaintext import --new mybook.gnucash chart-of-accounts.txt

Behaviour:
- --new + file does not exist: creates the file then imports
- --new + file already exists: UsageError (prevents accidental overwrite)
- --new + repo-level failure: created file is removed (no orphaned files)
- --new + --dry-run: UsageError (mutually exclusive)
- without --new: existing behaviour unchanged, error now hints --new
- all path validation happens before create_new_file() is called

Account creation errors now tracked in result.errors/error_count instead of being silently logged, so callers see them in the import summary.

Fixture files added:
- tests/fixtures/import_new_with_transaction.txt
- tests/fixtures/import_new_accounts_only.txt
- tests/fixtures/import_new_invalid_account_type.txt

Tests added (use fixtures, no inline plaintext):
- test_import_new_creates_file
- test_import_new_accounts_only (accounts-only plaintext still imports)
- test_import_new_fails_if_exists
- test_import_without_new_still_requires_existing_file
- test_import_new_and_dry_run_are_mutually_exclusive
- test_import_new_reports_account_creation_error

Pre-commit hook updated:
- AI review now only runs when lint + tests both pass (saves tokens)
- Tests now run via test-all-versions-parallel.sh (all 4 versions)
- Lint/test failures block immediately without waiting for AI review

test-all-versions-parallel.sh fixes:
- Exclude .ruff_cache from rsync (root-owned from prior Docker runs)
- Cleanup uses Docker alpine to remove root-owned files before rm -rf

author: copilot
body:
Runs the browser-compatibility skill against the repo to measure, decide, and enforce browser support across all three compatibility dimensions: CSS features, JS syntax, and JS APIs.

## Findings (Phase 1 — build output)

| Dimension | Result | Effective floor |
|---|---|---|
| CSS features | ⚠️ Inconclusive | Safari 16.4+, Chrome 111+ (Tailwind v4 hardcoded) |
| JS syntax | ✅ ES2022 floor | Chrome 94+, Firefox 93+, Safari 15+ |
| JS APIs | ✅ Pass | `baseline widely available` — no gaps |

**CSS note:** Both `doiuse` and `lightningcss-cli` crash on Tailwind v4's emitted `@layer properties { @supports (...) { } }` syntax — this is a parser limitation, not a compatibility failure. Tailwind v4's hardcoded floor aligns with `baseline widely available`, so no conflict exists.

**JS syntax note:** Floor is ES2022 (not ES2023 baseline) due to private class fields `#` in bundled dependencies — acceptable, as ES2022 ⊂ ES2023 target.

## Enforcement added (Phase 3)

**3A — source-level (editor/lint-time):**
- `.stylelintrc.json` — new; `stylelint-no-unsupported-browser-features` targeting `baseline widely available` with explicit mobile browsers (`and_chr`, `and_ff`, `ios_saf`)
- `eslint.config.mjs` — compat rule now scoped to `app/**` source files instead of globally
- `lint:compat` script — `eslint . && stylelint "**/*.css"`

**3B — build-output scripts (CI regression gates):**
- `eslint.compat-check.mjs` — dedicated ESLint config for checking build output APIs
- `compat:syntax` — `es-check es2022 ".next/static/chunks/**/*.js"` (catches dep upgrades that raise the syntax floor)
- `compat:apis` — `eslint --config eslint.compat-check.mjs ".next/static/chunks/**/*.js"`
- `compat:css` / `compat:css:lightning` intentionally omitted — no reliable emitted-CSS tool works on this stack

## Pre-existing foundations
`.browserslistrc` (`baseline widely available`), `eslint-plugin-compat`, and `es-check` were already present — this PR wires them into a consistent enforcement workflow and fills the missing Stylelint layer.

## Parent Issue Context

## Original Request

> Analyze entire frontend codebase, ensure that Light/Dark theme align with app style and theme. Ensure that ALL components and elements in app have proper contrast in both Light and Dark theme for best UI UX. @Medium

## User Story

As a frontend developer and UX stakeholder on Project Solune, I want the entire frontend codebase analyzed to ensure Light and Dark themes are consistent with the app's style and visual identity, so that every component and UI element has proper color contrast in both modes, delivering the best possible UI/UX experience for all users.

## UI/UX Description

Conduct a full visual and code audit of every component, page, and UI element across the application in both Light and Dark theme modes. All text, icons, borders, backgrounds, inputs, modals, tooltips, badges, buttons, cards, and interactive states (hover, focus, disabled, active) must meet or exceed WCAG 2.1 AA contrast ratios (minimum 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and UI components). Theme tokens and CSS variables must be consistently applied — no hardcoded colors that break in either mode. Dark theme backgrounds should avoid pure black (#000) in favor of elevated surface colors that match the app's design language, and Light theme backgrounds should avoid pure white where it creates harshness. All theme transitions (if animated) should be smooth and consistent. Components must never appear unthemed, broken, or visually mismatched in either mode. The audit should also verify that third-party or custom component library elements adopt the correct theme context and are not rendering with default or mismatched styles.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST audit every frontend component and page to verify correct application of Light and Dark theme tokens/CSS variables with no hardcoded color values that bypass the theming system.
- System MUST ensure all text-to-background contrast ratios meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards (≥4.5:1 for body/small text, ≥3:1 for large text, headings, and UI component boundaries) in both Light and Dark modes.
- System MUST verify and fix all interactive element states — hover, focus, active, disabled — to have visible and appropriately contrasted styling in both themes.
- System MUST ensure that all component variants (buttons, badges, alerts, inputs, modals, tooltips, cards, navigation, sidebars, dropdowns) render correctly and are visually consistent with the overall app style in both Light and Dark modes.
- System MUST align all theme colors and design tokens with the established Project Solune app style guide, removing any stale, inconsistent, or conflicting color definitions.
- System SHOULD audit and correct any third-party or embedded component library elements that may not correctly inherit the active theme context.
- System SHOULD document any new or updated design tokens introduced during the audit (variable names, Light/Dark values) to maintain a living style reference.
- System MUST verify that theme-switching (toggling between Light and Dark) does not produce visual glitches, unstyled flashes (FOUC), or broken layouts on any page or component.

## Technical Notes

Perform a systematic file-by-file review of all frontend components, likely under src/components, src/pages, or equivalent directories, checking for hardcoded hex/rgb values and ensuring all color usage references shared theme tokens (CSS custom properties, Tailwind theme config, or equivalent theming system in use). Use automated contrast-checking tools (e.g., axe-core, Storybook a11y addon, or a custom script using the WCAG contrast algorithm) to programmatically flag failing elements rather than relying solely on manual review. Pay special attention to overlay layers, skeleton loaders, scrollbars, code blocks, and any SVG/icon fills that may not respond to theme context. Ensure the theming mechanism (context provider, CSS class on root, data attribute, etc.) is correctly scoped and inherited throughout the entire component tree with no isolated subtrees that escape theme control.

---

## 📋 Standard PR Informationen

`wundabzuege` is stored as a negative number by `_calculateWounds` (e.g. `-2` for 3 wounds), but `_applyActorModifiers` applied it via `-=`, turning the penalty into a bonus for AT, VT, and FK.

## Root Cause

```js
// Before: -= (-2) == +2 → increases AT/VT/FK (bug)
system.computed.at -= wundabzuege
system.computed.modifiers.at.push(`Wunden: -${wundabzuege}`) // displays "Wunden: --2"
```

## Fix

```js
// After: += (-2) == -2 → decreases AT/VT/FK (correct)
system.computed.at += wundabzuege
system.computed.modifiers.at.push(`Wunden: ${wundabzuege}`) // displays "Wunden: -2"
```

Same fix applied to `vt` and `fk`. Test mocks updated from `wundabzuege: 2` → `wundabzuege: -2` to match actual actor data shape from `_calculateWounds`. An additional FK assertion (`expect(weapon.system.computed.fk).toBe(-4)`) was added to the wound penalty test to catch regressions on the FK wound modifier sign.

author: futurethang
body:
## Summary

Introduces a three-tier game mode system that allows players to choose their experience level per session. All tiers share the same core dice-and-stats engine but unlock progressively more control over team composition and in-game decisions. This is infrastructure-only: Arcade mode maintains feature parity with current behavior, while Team Builder and Manager tiers are defined and selectable with gated stubs for future mechanics (fatigue, platoon splits, situational modifiers).

## Key Changes

**Documentation & Architecture**
- Added `TIER-ARCHITECTURE.md` — comprehensive developer guide covering tier profiles, gating patterns, data model changes, and testing strategy
- Added `EXPERIENCE-TIERS.md` — player-facing tier definitions (Arcade, Team Builder, Manager Mode)
- Added `TIER-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` — step-by-step implementation checklist
- Updated `FUTURE-ROADMAP.md` to align with tier-driven feature prioritization

**Shared Types (`contracts/`)**
- Created `contracts/tier.ts` with `GameTier`, `TierProfile`, and `TIER_PROFILES` constant
- Exported tier types from `contracts/index.d.ts` for use by both frontend and backend
- Tier profiles define: team source (preset/custom), salary cap, roster size, allowed in-game decisions, and enabled engine modifiers

**Backend Game Engine**
- Extended `resolveAtBat()` signature to accept optional `rules: TierProfile` and `gameContext: GameContext` parameters
- Added `GameContext` interface for situational state (pitcher at-bat count, handedness, runners, outs)
- Implemented stub modifier functions (`calculateFatigueModifier`, `applyPlatoonModifier`, `applySituationalModifier`) that return 1.0 (no-op) — ready for future implementation
- All 123 existing engine tests pass unchanged; Arcade mode has zero overhead from Manager Mode features

**Backend Game Service & Routes**
- Extended `createGame()` to accept optional `tier` parameter (defaults to 'arcade')
- Game object now stores `tier: GameTier` and `rules: TierProfile` snapshot at creation time
- POST `/api/games` route accepts optional `tier` field in request body
- Added tier-based action validation in `recordMove()` (rejects pinch hits/pitching changes if rules disallow)
- Extended `validateRosterForTier()` to check roster size against tier requirements

**Frontend Types & Components**
- Duplicated tier types in `frontend/src/types/index.ts` for pre-game contexts (team building, tier selection)
- Created `FeatureGate.tsx` component for conditional rendering based on tier rules
- Updated `Play.tsx` to accept `selectedTier` state and pass to game creation API
- Updated `Game.tsx` to import and use `FeatureGate` for tier-gated UI sections
- Updated `gameStore.ts` and `useGameSession.ts` to handle tier/rules from game state

**WebSocket**
- `game:state` event now includes `tier` and `rules` fields
- Clients receive tier configuration at game start, enabling client-side feature gating

**Testing**
- Added comprehensive `tier.test.ts` with 40+ tests covering:
  - Tier profile definitions and invariants
  - Tier validation helpers (`isValidTier`, `getTierProfile`)
  - Tier-aware engine behavior (modifiers enabled/disabled per tier)
  - Roster validation against tier requirements
- Updated `game-routes.test.ts` with tier-aware game creation tests

## Implementation Details

- **Single source of truth**: `TIER_PROFILES` constant is the only place tier behavior is defined; all components and services read from it
- **Backward compatible**: Arcade mode behaves identically to current behavior; existing tests pass without modification
- **Server-authoritative**: Backend validates all tier-based actions; hacked clients cannot bypass tier restrictions
- **Snapshot at creation**: Game stores a frozen copy of tier rules at creation time, preventing mid-game rule drift if tier definitions change between app versions
- **No code branching**: Tier differences expressed as configuration (feature flags + parameters), not `if/else` forks scattered

predict_newdata() rebuilds task$col_info from the new backend, which
recomputes factor levels from the raw data. This can discard the canonical
level ordering set by TaskClassif$positive<-.

Columns marked with fix_factor_levels = TRUE indicate that their level
ordering must be preserved (e.g. the target column in binary classification).

This patch restores the levels field from the training task for those columns
when rebuilding task$col_info.

A regression test is added to ensure predict_newdata() preserves the same
probability ordering as predict().

All existing tests pass.

### Motivation
- Make the operator `doctor` command deterministic, machine-consumable, and operationally useful for automation and triage.
- Surface clear PASS/DEGRADED/FAIL semantics with remediation text so operators can act without guessing.
- Record a concise verification audit and evidence from the final go-live flip pass to document what changed and why.

### Description
- Replaced and refactored `scripts/doctor.mjs` to emit structured per-check tuples (`subsystem`, `status`, `message`, `remediation`), compute a global summary (`PASS|DEGRADED|FAIL`), support `--json` output, and add operator flags `--include-pipeline` and `--skip-kernel-health` for controlled runs.
- Reworked checks to be lightweight by default (env presence, URL shape, workspace integrity, kernel health) and make pipeline gates optional to avoid expensive default runs.
- Updated operator documentation to document canonical `pnpm run settler:doctor` usage, deterministic semantics, JSON mode, and flag guidance (`docs/setup/operator-runbook.md` and `docs/capabilities.md`).
- Added a final go-live flip audit and execution evidence log documenting the pass and verification commands (`docs/launch/final-go-live-flip-audit-2026-03-12.md`, `evidence/final-go-live-flip/command-log.txt`).
- Files changed: `scripts/doctor.mjs`, `docs/setup/operator-runbook.md`, `docs/capabilities.md`, `docs/launch/final-go-live-flip-audit-2026-03-12.md`, and `evidence/final-go-live-flip/command-log.txt`.

### Testing
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` — PASS.
- `pnpm run settler:doctor` — FAIL (expected in this environment due to missing Supabase/database env); the command returns non-zero on `FAIL` as designed.
- `pnpm run settler:doctor -- --json --skip-kernel-health` — FAIL with deterministic JSON output verified (missing required envs surfaced without secrets).
- `pnpm run kernel:health` and Rust checks — `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --all` all PASSED; kernel reports explicit degraded/disabled mode as expected.
- `pnpm run verify:setup` — FAIL (expected missing env in container).
- Long-running monorepo gates (`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm run check:production`) were exercised but did not complete within bounded run windows in this environment and are classified as NON_BLOCKING_FRICTION in the attached audit evidence.

### Motivation

- Provide a single, maintainable Go-based load testing tool to exercise SIP control messages, RTP file transfers (UDP/TCP) and A-side HTTP invokes for regression and performance validation. 
- Allow parameterized runs (concurrency, QPS, file size, transfer mode, duration) and produce both per-request and aggregate outputs that are easy for humans to read and for automation to compare. 
- Integrate the tool into the repo so it can be versioned, built and run alongside the gateway service and CI/tests.

### Description

- Added a reusable load test engine at `gateway-server/loadtest` implementing operations for `sip-command-create`, `sip-status-receipt`, `rtp-udp-upload`, `rtp-tcp-upload` and `http-invoke`, with aggregation of throughput, success rate, P50/P95/P99 and error-type distribution, and outputs `results.jsonl` + `summary.json` per run. 
- Added a CLI wrapper at `gateway-server/cmd/loadtest` with flags for targets, `-concurrency`, `-qps`, `-file-size`, `-chunk-size`, `-transfer-mode`, `-duration`, addresses/URL, `-output-dir` and `-timeout`, plus `normalizeTargets`/mode filtering. 
- Added convenience script `scripts/loadtest/run.sh`, documentation `docs/loadtest-toolkit.md`, updated `README.md` entry and `gateway-server/Makefile` targets `build-loadtest`/`run-loadtest`. 
- Added unit tests for key logic: `TestPercentile`, `TestValidateConfig`, `TestClassifyErr` (in `gateway-server/loadtest/loadtest_test.go`) and `TestNormalizeTargetsByMode` (in `gateway-server/cmd/loadtest/main_test.go`).

### Testing

- Ran the full backend test suite with `cd gateway-server && go test ./...` and all tests (including the new loadtest unit tests) passed. 
- Verified the CLI help and startup with `cd gateway-server && go run ./cmd/loadtest -h` which printed usage as expected. 
- The loadtest run writes `results.jsonl` and `summary.json` under the configured `-output-dir/<run_id>/` for downstream analysis and comparison.

### Motivation
- Remove an operator footgun where callers were forced to include `CANNOT_UNWRAP` in their `ownerControlledFuses` despite the contract already forcing that fuse. 
- Improve safety and coverage around activation/registration/resolver flows so operator behavior is predictable and auditable. 
- Improve operator UX and CI hygiene so non-technical operators have clear runbooks and CI verifies type correctness.

### Description
- Removed the `InvalidOwnerControlledFuses` check and the `_validateOwnerControlledFuses` call so callers may pass owner fuses without needing to include `CANNOT_UNWRAP`, while the contract still forces `CANNOT_UNWRAP` in the produced child fuses. (contract change)
- Added unit tests covering inactive-parent rejection, owner-controlled fuse passthrough, resolver-record forwarding success, and resolver-record namehash mismatch reverts to cover previously-missing behavior paths. (tests)
- Enhanced the `scripts/register-subname.ts` CLI with `--help`/usage output and clearer error behavior when required args are missing. (script change)
- Expanded the README into an explicit operator runbook with clearer ENS expiry semantics, troubleshooting, deployment and operator checklists. (docs)
- Added a TypeScript `typecheck` step to the CI workflow so PRs validate static types in addition to build/test. (CI)

- Ran `npm run typecheck` (i.e. `tsc --noEmit`) which completed successfully.

body:
The guiservice topology tab always showed "❌ Error: gtopt_diagram not available" because `scripts/gtopt_diagram/__init__.py` only exported `main`, while `app.py` imported `FilterOptions`, `TopologyBuilder`, and `model_to_visjs` directly from the package — causing an `ImportError` even when the scripts were properly pip-installed.

Additionally, `guiservice/CMakeLists.txt` never installed the `gtopt_diagram` package, so the directory that `app.py` adds to `sys.path` (`share/gtopt/scripts/`) didn't exist after `cmake --install`.

## Changes

- **`scripts/gtopt_diagram/__init__.py`** — re-export the three symbols required by the guiservice:
  ```python
  from .gtopt_diagram import (  # noqa: F401
      FilterOptions,
      TopologyBuilder,
      main,
      model_to_visjs,
  )
  ```

- **`guiservice/CMakeLists.txt`** — add an `install(DIRECTORY ...)` rule that copies `scripts/gtopt_diagram/*.py` to `share/gtopt/scripts/gtopt_diagram/`, which is the path `app.py` already adds to `sys.path`. Guarded by a check for `gtopt_diagram/gtopt_diagram.py` (the actual implementation file). Applies to both standalone guiservice builds and the `all` super-project.

author: mirka
body:
## What?

Adds a custom ESLint rule, `@wordpress/no-unmerged-classname`, and enables it for `packages/ui/src/`.

## Why?

In `@wordpress/ui`, components that spread rest props onto a JSX element can silently drop the consumer-supplied `className` if it isn't properly merged. For example:

```jsx
function Foo( { padding, ...restProps } ) {
    return <div { ...restProps } className={ styles.foo } />;
}
```

Here, any `className` passed by the consumer is in `restProps`, but the explicit `className` after the spread silently overwrites it. The correct pattern is to destructure `className` and merge it (e.g. via `clsx`).

This is a subtle mistake — the code looks reasonable and TypeScript won't flag it. A lint rule catches it at authoring time.

## How?

The rule flags any JSX element that has both an explicit `className` attribute and a spread attribute, where the enclosing function's props parameter doesn't destructure `className`. It handles:

- Object destructuring with rest element (`{ padding, ...rest }`) — flags if `className` is not among the destructured properties.
- Plain identifier params (`props`) — flags if the identifier is spread directly onto the element.
- Components that forward `className` to a different element than the one with the spread (e.g. the Tooltip pattern) — not flagged, since `className` is destructured.

The rule is not included in any preset. It's enabled for `packages/ui/src/**` only, excluding test and story files.

## Testing Instructions

```bash
npm run test:unit -- --testPathPattern='packages/eslint-plugin/rules/__tests__/no-unmerged-classname'
```

This pull request introduces significant improvements and new features to the OEcon project, including a new GUI, enhanced CLI, parallelization plans, and better documentation. The changes modernize the user experience, add multi-session support, improve configuration handling, and lay out plans for future performance and flexibility enhancements. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme.

author: emmanash-bod
body:
**Root cause:** Vercel's build cache restores `node_modules` without re-running `postinstall`, so `prisma generate` never executes. The auto-generated `vercel-build` script only runs `next build`, skipping Prisma client generation entirely.

**Error:**
```
Module not found: Can't resolve '@/generated/prisma/client'
Error: Command "npm run vercel-build" exited with 1
```

**Fix:** Add an explicit `vercel-build` script (`prisma generate && next build`) so the Prisma client is always generated before the Next.js build, regardless of cache state.

One-line change in `package.json`.

author: claudiaann1
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a simple recursive implementation that computes and prints the Nth line of Pascal's Triangle using arrays to store each line.
- Meet the requirement that each interior value is the sum of the two values above it and that line numbering is 1-based.
- Include minimal input validation and readable output formatting for interactive use.

### Description
- Add `PascalTriangleRecursive.java` which reads an integer `N` from standard input and validates that `N` is positive.
- Implement `getPascalLine(int n)` as a recursive function with base case `n == 1` returning `{1}` and recursive construction of the current line from the previous line.
- Construct each line in an `int[]` with `1` at the ends and interior values computed by `previousLine[i-1] + previousLine[i]`.
- Add `printLine(int[] line)` to print the computed line values space-separated followed by a newline.

### Testing
- Run `javac PascalTriangleRecursive.java` to compile, which completed successfully.
- Run `printf '6\n' | java PascalTriangleRecursive` which executed and produced the expected 6th line output (`1 5 10 10 5 1`).

author: christiaan-ph
body:
Add `allowClear` to LemonSelect for list-type HogQL variables in both view/dashboard mode and edit popover mode. This lets users clear a selected list variable back to null, which is needed for optional variables (e.g. filtering by channel type).

The settings modal already had `allowClear` — this brings the runtime selectors in line.

## Problem

When using a list-type HogQL variable in a SQL insight, there's no way to clear a selected value once one has been chosen. This is fine for required variables (e.g. granularity in a time series), but for optional variables (e.g. channel type to segment conversion rates) users have no way to return to an unfiltered/non-segmented view. The current workaround is to use a string variable instead.

## Changes

- Added `allowClear` prop to `LemonSelect` for list variables in **view/dashboard mode** (`VariableComponent`)
- Added `allowClear` prop to `LemonSelect` for list variables in **edit popover mode** (`VariableInput`)
- When the user clears the selection, `isNull` is set to `true` so the variable correctly resolves to null in the query

Both changes are in `frontend/src/queries/nodes/DataVisualization/Components/Variables/Variables.tsx`. The `ListDefaultField` in `VariableFields.tsx` (settings modal) already had `allowClear` — this brings the runtime UI in line.

## How did you test this code?

Manual testing steps:
1. Create a SQL insight with a list-type variable
2. Select a value from the list
3. Verify the X button now appears to clear the selection
4. Clear the selection and confirm the query re-runs with a null variable value

## Publish to changelog?

no

## 🤖 LLM context

Co-authored with Claude Code (Opus 4.6).

- Support a new 'Ion' therapy flag end-to-end and expose it across UI, DB, and sync layers. 
- Improve touch/mobile interactions (single-tap behavior), step selection/swapping, and tablet/phone ergonomics to avoid double-tap reliability issues. 
- Harden realtime / polling / undo flows to prevent ghost/replay/stale-bed states and make bed↔log synchronization more resilient. 
- Expand patient-log capabilities (search/import, grid selection, clipboard, richer edit behaviors) and add developer conveniences (auto-push setup, rollout playbook).

## Summary

- Seat counting in `handleSubscriptionEventInternal` was summing quantities from ALL Stripe subscription line items, including non-seat products (KiloPass, KiloClaw, add-ons). This inflated seat counts when subscriptions contained mixed product types.
- Added `isSeatLineItem` filter that checks each line item's `price.product` against the known seat product IDs (`STRIPE_TEAMS_SUBSCRIPTION_PRODUCT_ID` and `STRIPE_ENTERPRISE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRODUCT_ID`). Both `seatCount` and `amountUsd` now only aggregate from seat-related line items.
- Updated mock subscription in tests to use the real teams product ID, and added two new tests covering mixed seat/non-seat subscriptions and multi-price seat subscriptions with add-ons.

## Verification

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — passes with no errors
- [x] Existing tests verified to not regress (test failures are pre-existing DB connection issues in sandbox, identical before and after change)
- [x] Manual review of all callers of `handleSubscriptionEvent` and `handleSubscriptionEventInternal` to confirm no downstream impact

## Visual Changes

N/A

## Reviewer Notes

- The `SEAT_PRODUCT_IDS` set is built at module load time from env vars, with `.filter(Boolean)` to handle cases where an env var might be empty.
- `isSeatLineItem` checks `typeof productId !== 'string'` to handle the case where Stripe returns an expanded `Product` object rather than a string ID — in that case, the item is conservatively excluded. In practice, subscription items always have string product IDs unless explicitly expanded.
- The `firstLineItem` (used for period start/end dates) still uses the first item from ALL line items, not just seat items. This is intentional — all items in a subscription share the same billing period.

author: ericmariasis
body:
## Summary

  This PR adds the minimum Story 81 evidence and ingress health metric pack needed before the AI bridge. It exposes one narrow
  creator-scoped read surface for the highest-risk hardening seams without changing any canonical truth contracts or widening
  scope into broader Phase 14 observability work.

  ## What Changed

  - Added a new `evidence_ingress_health` service that aggregates creator-scoped health signals from existing hardening seams.
  - Added `GET /reports/health` as the minimal inspection surface for these signals.
  - Added reporting schemas for the health response contract.
  - Added structured logging on health reads via `reports_health_snapshot`.
  - Added focused degraded-case coverage for the new service and route.

  The health snapshot currently reports:

  - Booking attribution gaps:
    - unattributed booking count
    - unattributed reason counts
  - Calendly ingress health:
    - backlog event count for creator-resolvable in-flight states
    - failed event count
    - status counts
  - Payment provenance health:
    - settled state counts
    - current backlog event count
    - current backlog reason counts
  - Blocked billing health:
    - open blocked billing case count
    - blocked reason counts
  - Authoritative content lag:
    - lagging content count only where lag is unambiguous
    - lag reason counts

  ## Why

  Story 81 is intended to make the new evidence and ingress hardening seams visible enough for support and later beta-
  readiness work while staying intentionally narrow.

  This PR maps each signal directly to an existing seam rather than inventing new generic telemetry:

  - booking attribution current state
  - verified Calendly ingress journal processing state
  - settled payment provenance diagnostics
  - blocked billing backlog
  - authoritative content promotion lag

  The implementation preserves already-settled Story 66-70 and Story 77-80 semantics, including:

  - invoice-backed settled truth remains canonical
  - provider-side unmatched/conflicting signals remain diagnostic
  - booking attribution authority remains unchanged
  - Calendly ingress continues to use the persist-only ingress plus shared reducer path
  - authoritative content authority remains tied to `Content.authoritative_extraction_artifact_id`

  ## Validation

  Ran:

  - `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m py_compile app\services\evidence_ingress_health.py app\api\reports.py
  app\schemas\reporting.py tests\test_evidence_ingress_health.py`
  - `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q tests\test_evidence_ingress_health.py tests\test_reports_summary.py
  tests\test_settled_paid_evidence.py tests\test_authoritative_content_evidence.py tests\test_calendly_webhooks.py
  tests\test_phase12_validation.py tests\test_ui_auth_shell.py`

  Result:

  - `76 passed in 73.26s`

  Manual verification also confirmed that representative degraded cases emit the expected health signals via `GET /reports/
  health`, including:

  - missing attribution
  - failed Calendly ingress event
  - payment provenance backlog
  - blocked billing backlog
  - authoritative content lag

  ## Risks / Follow-ups

  - This PR intentionally stops at one small read seam plus structured logs. It does not add dashboards, alerts, or runbooks.
  - The `/reports/health` contract is narrow by design; if support or beta-readiness needs expand, additional surfaces should
  build from this seam rather than redefining the underlying semantics.
  - Manual verification depends on pinned local auth/test env settings, especially matching `JWT_ALGORITHM` and `JWT_SECRET`
  between the app process and token-minting shell.

  Validation summary for the PR body:

  - Added one narrow creator-scoped health snapshot surface instead of broader observability work.
  - Covered representative degraded cases with focused tests and related regressions.
  - Manual verification succeeded against a clean local server with pinned test auth settings.

  Known risk / follow-up note to keep handy:

  - The biggest operational footgun in manual verification is env drift between the running server and the token-generation
    shell.

The following PR removes react-dom/server renderToStaticMarkup from copy grid elements of Grid to favour the recommended createRoot approach suggested by React's official documentation, because react dom's server version is not recommended by react themselves and shouldn't be surfacing publicly in the context of a component library.

body:
Three independent misconfigurations caused all CI runs on `main` to fail.

## Issues & Fixes

- **`ci-workflow.yml` ran from repo root** — `package.json` lives in `app/`, not the root. Added `defaults: run: working-directory: app` and an `Enable Corepack` step (required for `"packageManager": "yarn@4.13.0"`).

- **`deploy.yml` enabled Corepack too late** — `Setup Node.js` with `cache: "yarn"` calls `yarn cache dir` using system Yarn 1.x, which hard-errors on the `packageManager` field before Corepack is ever activated. Moved `Enable Corepack` to before the `Setup Node.js` step.

- **`app/package.json` had no `test` script** — `yarn test` in CI had nothing to invoke. Added `"test": "next lint"` as the CI test entry point.

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/ci-workflow.yml` — set `defaults.run.working-directory: app`, add `corepack enable` before `yarn install`
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — move `Enable Corepack` step above `Setup Node.js`
- `app/package.json` — add `"test": "next lint"`

## Summary

Implements a browser-backed local storage filesystem with package support and replaces the previous in-memory filesystem. Introduces a layered filesystem abstraction (temporary vs local), integrates a JS-backed filesystem proxy into the WebAssembly runtime, and updates the frontend to use the new FS API.

### WASM runtime
- Runtime entry point changed from run(path) to run(fsProxy, path) to accept a browser-provided filesystem proxy.
- Added NewLocalStorageFS (wasm/local_storage_fs.go) to initialize a JS-backed local storage filesystem that delegates file, directory, and metadata operations to a JS proxy.
- Adjusted startup and error handling to surface filesystem-related failures cleanly.

### Filesystem core
- Added a typed FS interface (open, stat, readDir, writeFile, remove, move, mkdirAll).
- Implemented AbstractFS (in-memory tree), EphemeralFS (seedable temp FS), LocalStorageFS (persistence to localStorage), and LayeredFS (namespaced composition exposing /tmp and /local).
- Added FileNode type and path utilities; example generator output and example files are wrapped under /tmp to align with the layered layout.

### Frontend state & provider
- Replaced the prior flat file-store with a hierarchical file-tree-store (Zustand) managing temp/local trees, active file state (with dirty tracking), expansion state, and file operations (create/rename/delete/move/save).
- Added FSProvider and useFS to provide LayeredFS to the React tree and open a default file on initialization.

### UI and integration
- Updated Editor, AppSidebar, and related components to integrate with the new FS API and provider.
- Added FileTreeDialog and several UI primitives (DropdownMenu, Dialog) used by the sidebar and dialogs.
- Editor run/save flows now operate against the layered FS; examples moved under /tmp.

### Tooling and types
- Switched tooling from ESLint to Biome and added formatting/lint scripts; added Immer dependency.
- Updated TypeScript typings: window.run now accepts an FS proxy and window.updateFile was removed; wasm-related type declarations updated.
- useBallerina hook now integrates FS and no longer exposes updateFile.

### Outcome
- Provides persistent, namespaced filesystem support in the browser, aligns the frontend and wasm runtime with a JS proxy-backed FS, and enables package-level operations (create package scaffolding and manage files across temp/local namespaces).
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

body:
**Problem**: The `github.com/astaxie/beego` dependency was used solely for its in-memory cache, but it pulled in **153 transitive dependency entries** in `go.sum` (redis, memcache, protobuf, prometheus, various database drivers, etc.).

**Solution**: Replaced it with a minimal ~50-line `cache/cache.go` implementation that provides thread-safe in-memory key-value storage with optional per-item TTL -- the only features actually used from beego.

**Changes made**:
- **`cache/cache.go`** (new) -- Simple `sync.RWMutex`-based cache with `Get`, `Put` (with TTL), and `Delete`
- **`client/auth.go`** -- Switched import from beego to local cache; simplified code by removing nil-checks and error handling that are no longer needed (our cache always initializes and operations can't fail)
- **`client/client.go`** -- Switched import; replaced exported `AccountCache`/`URLCache` (of which `AccountCache` was unused) with a single unexported `urlCache`; removed `initialiseCaches()` function
- **`client/client_core.go`** -- Removed `initialiseCaches()` call and unused `logging` import
- **`client/client_test.go`**, **`client/client_core_test.go`** -- Removed `initialiseCaches()` calls and unused `log` import
- **`go.mod`** -- Removed `github.com/astaxie/beego v1.12.3`
- **`go.sum`** -- Went from 159 lines down to 6 (**153 transitive dependencies removed**)

Fixes #139

author: gonzaddv
body:
## Summary

- `cmd_kill`: `cd "$bare_dir"` was called unconditionally, crashing with `set -euo pipefail` when the bare repo directory no longer exists. Now guards both the worktree removal and the prune/branch-delete steps with `[ -d "$bare_dir" ]`. If the worktree directory exists but the bare repo is gone, falls back to plain `rm -rf`.
- `cmd_gc`: Separated the `bare_dir` and `worktree_path` existence checks so that: (a) if only `bare_dir` exists, we still run `git worktree prune` to clean up stale metadata; (b) if only `worktree_path` exists, we remove it directly; (c) if neither exists, we skip silently and proceed to unregister.

In both cases the session is always unregistered from the port registry, so no orphaned entries remain.

author: pataforista
body:
### Motivation
- Alinear la interfaz con una estética de app de recetas más orgánica y cálida usando tonos tierra y un layout tipo “Bento Grid”.
- Mejorar la jerarquía visual y la profundidad de las tarjetas/paneles sin añadir ruido visual.
- Hacer las interacciones más táctiles con micro-feedback (hover/active) para una mejor experiencia en móvil y escritorio.

### Description
- Actualicé los tokens de color en `:root` dentro de `styles.css` para introducir la paleta earth-tone (moss, terracota, crema) y ajustar neutrales y contenedores. 
- Refiné header y paneles con mezcla de superficie (`color-mix`), `backdrop-filter` (glassmorphism sutil), radios más grandes (`border-radius: 26px`) y sombras suaves para dar profundidad sin saturar la UI. 
- Añadí micro-interacciones en botones con transformaciones `hover`/`active` y ajustes de transición para sensación de “lift” y “press`. 
- Implementé comportamiento tipo Bento Grid en escritorio con un `@media (min-width: 960px)` que distribuye `#view-today` en cuatro columnas, hace que `#panel-context` y `#panel-inventory` ocupen bloques equilibrados y fuerza `#resultsPanel` a ancho completo.
- Ajusté fondos y gradientes para mayor coherencia visual (actualización de `background-image`) y pequeñas mejoras de espaciado (`gap`) en vistas activas.

### Testing
- Ejecuté `npm run build` y la compilación de producción completó correctamente (se generó `dist/` sin errores). 
- Levanté el servidor de desarrollo con `npm run dev` y Vite quedó disponible (servidor listo). 
- Validé visualmente mediante un script de Playwright que tomó una captura de `http://127.0.0.1:4173`, generando `artifacts/bento-earth-dashboard.png` correctamente.

author: kristianlorgen
body:
### Motivation
- The admin “Lag” panel could appear empty when a tournament created by the wizard had players in `players` but no rows in `teams`, making teams invisible in the UI despite players existing.
- Provide a backend-side, defensive recovery so the admin UI can render teams immediately without requiring manual repair.

### Description
- Updated `GET /api/admin/tournament/:id/teams` in `server.js` to fetch teams via helper functions and detect the empty-`teams` case for team-based formats.
- When a team-based tournament has no `teams` rows but has enough active `players`, the endpoint now groups players by the format `teamSize`, inserts `teams` rows, and creates corresponding `team_players` links inside a transaction.
- After rebuilding, the endpoint re-fetches teams and team_player links and returns the existing enriched response shape (`teams` + `tournament`) so the admin UI continues to work unchanged.
- This change is local to the teams endpoint and is a safe recovery path that only runs when teams are missing and enough active players exist.

### Testing
- Started the app with `npm start` and confirmed the server booted successfully (passed).
- Performed admin login via `POST /api/auth/admin-login` with the configured password and received success (passed).
- Created a tournament through the wizard by sending a `POST /api/admin/tournament-wizard` payload and confirmed both `players` and `teams` were created initially (passed).
- Simulated the broken state by deleting created `teams` via `DELETE /api/admin/team/:id` while leaving `players` intact, then called `GET /api/admin/tournament/1/teams` and verified the endpoint auto-recreated `teams` and `team_players` and returned the enriched teams payload (passed).
- All automated API checks above succeeded against the running server.

This PR introduces the `X-Pm-Encrypt-Untrusted` vCard field and refines the encryption preference logic across the Proton Web client monorepo to improve handling of WKD (Web Key Directory) contacts. The changes enable explicit user control over encryption to contacts whose keys are fetched from WKD and are therefore untrusted.

💡 **What:** Replaced the sequential `for` loop that updated parlay legs with a concurrent `Promise.all` and `.map` implementation.

author: copilot
body:
Auto-deploys on every push to `main` burn Netlify build minutes continuously. This adds a manual workflow to stop/resume Netlify builds on demand.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/netlify_toggle.yml`** — `workflow_dispatch` workflow with a `publier`/`depublier` dropdown. Calls the Netlify REST API to stop or resume auto-builds (`build_settings.stop_builds`); on `publier` also triggers an immediate deploy via `POST /builds`. Sets `permissions: {}` (no GITHUB_TOKEN scope needed). Requires two repo secrets: `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN` and `NETLIFY_SITE_ID`.

- **`netlify.toml`** — Declares the site as a zero-build static deployment (`command = ""`), publish dir at root, with a catch-all SPA redirect to `index.html`.

- **`README.md`** — Documents secret setup and workflow usage.

## Usage

In GitHub → **Actions** → **"Netlify - Publier / Dépublier"** → **Run workflow** → select action.

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `publier` | Enables auto-builds + triggers an immediate deploy |
| `depublier` | Stops auto-builds; live site stays up at current version |

## Required secrets

| Secret | Source |
|---|---|
| `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN` | app.netlify.com/user/applications → Personal access tokens |
| `NETLIFY_SITE_ID` | Site settings → General → Site ID |

author: rocky-d
body:
## Add dttb to Debugging Tools

**[dttb](https://github.com/rocky-d/dttb)** adds timestamps to Python exception tracebacks with a single line of code.

```python
import dttb; dttb.apply()
```

After that one line, every traceback includes the exact timestamp when the exception occurred:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...at 2024-01-15 03:47:22.341 UTC
RuntimeError: something went wrong
```

**Features:**
- Patches both `sys.excepthook` and `threading.excepthook`
- Timezone configuration support
- Custom callbacks
- Zero dependencies

Invaluable for debugging long-running services, async apps, and multi-threaded programs where you need to know _when_ an error occurred, not just _that_ it occurred.

**Links:**
- GitHub: https://github.com/rocky-d/dttb
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/dttb/
- Docs: https://rocky-d.github.io/dttb/

# Integration Rede for GiveWP

Contribuidores: linknacional  
Link: https://www.linknacional.com.br/wordpress/  
Tags: givewp, pagamento, rede, crédito, débito, gateway  
Testado até: 3.0  
Versão estável: 2.0.9  
Licença: GPLv2 ou posterior  
URI da Licença: https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT  
Traduções: Português (Brasil) / Inglês

Integre o gateway de pagamento Rede ao GiveWP, permitindo doações via cartão de crédito e débito.

## Descrição

O Integration Rede for GiveWP oferece integração completa com o gateway de pagamento Rede, permitindo que sua plataforma de doações aceite pagamentos via:

- **Cartão de Crédito** (Rede)
- **Cartão de Débito** (Rede)

A [Rede](https://www.userede.com.br) é uma das principais adquirentes do Brasil, oferecendo soluções seguras e confiáveis para processamento de pagamentos.

**Recursos Principais**

- Sistema de parcelamento inteligente com cálculo de juros
- Validação 3DS para débito
- Cartão animado no checkout
- Suporte a reembolsos automáticos
- Logs detalhados de transações
- Compatibilidade com editor de blocos GiveWP

**Dependências**

Este plugin depende do GiveWP. Certifique-se de que o GiveWP está instalado e configurado antes de instalar o Integration Rede for GiveWP.

**Instruções de uso**

1. Procure na barra lateral do WordPress por 'Integration Rede for GiveWP'.
2. Nas opções do GiveWP, acesse 'Pagamentos' e configure o gateway disponível: 'Rede Crédito', 'Rede Débito'.
3. Configure as credenciais de API necessárias para o gateway.
4. Defina as opções de parcelamento, juros e limites conforme necessário.
5. Salve as configurações.

Pronto! Seus doadores poderão contribuir via Rede com cartão de crédito e débito.

1. Baixe o plugin.
2. No painel administrativo do WordPress, vá para Plugins > Adicionar Novo.
3. Clique em "Enviar Plugin" e selecione o arquivo ZIP do plugin que você baixou.

author: lucasmachine
body:
## Problem

Some translated strings are not applied because the extracted `msgid` is missing a leading byte that exists in the game data.

This was reproduced with the RPG Maker 2000/2003 game **水たまりの彼女**.  
In affected event messages, a leading **DEL (`0x7F`)** byte is present in map data, but was removed during extraction, so EasyRPG Player could not match the translation and fell back to original Japanese text.

## Root Cause

`Utils::RemoveControlChars` removed both:
- C0 control bytes (`0x00-0x1F`)
- DEL (`0x7F`)

For this game, DEL (`0x7F`) is meaningful as a message prefix, so removing it causes `msgid` mismatch.

## Fix

Keep DEL (`0x7F`) in extracted strings, while still removing C0 control bytes (`0x00-0x1F`).

### Scope

- No CLI changes
- No API changes
- Minimal behavior change in extraction normalization only

## Changed File

- `lcftrans/src/utils.cpp`
  - `Utils::RemoveControlChars`: stop removing `0x7F`, continue removing `0x00-0x1F`
  - updated comment to clarify behavior

## Verification

- Reproduced against **水たまりの彼女**
- Confirmed affected extracted `msgid` now keeps the leading DEL byte
- Confirmed translations are now correctly applied in EasyRPG Player for those lines

author: deramangos64-cloud
body:
# Research Collaboration Network Smart Contract

## Summary

This pull request adds a blockchain-based research collaboration platform that incentivizes open data sharing through tokenized rewards. The system allows researchers to register datasets, participate in peer validation, and earn tokens based on contribution quality and community engagement.

## Key Components

### Dataset Management
- Register research datasets with comprehensive metadata (title, description, category, access URI)
- Support for six research categories: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science, Medicine, and Social Sciences
- Public/private access control for datasets
- Immutable contribution tracking ensures proper attribution

### Token Rewards System
- Dynamic reward calculation based on peer validation scores
- Three-tier reward multipliers (1x, 2x, 3x) based on validation quality
- Configurable validation threshold for reward eligibility
- Rate-limited claims to prevent abuse
- Managed reward pool with administrative controls

### Peer Validation
- Community-driven quality assurance through peer review
- Rating system (1-5 scale) for dataset validation
- Prevention of self-validation and duplicate validations
- Validator reputation tracking
- Validation scores directly influence reward distribution

### Researcher Profiles
- Automatic profile creation on first interaction
- Token balance management
- Contribution and validation history tracking
- Reputation scoring based on participation
- Transfer capability between researchers

## Technical Details

### Data Structures
- **datasets map**: Stores complete dataset information including metadata, validation metrics, and access statistics
- **researcher-profiles map**: Manages user balances, contributions, validations, and reputation
- **dataset-validations map**: Tracks validator participation to prevent duplicate reviews
- **dataset-access-log map**: Records access patterns for usage analytics
- **category-stats map**: Aggregates statistics per research category
- **pending-rewards map**: Holds rewards awaiting claim

### Public Functions
- `register-dataset`: Submit new research data with metadata
- `validate-dataset`: Peer review existing datasets with quality ratings
- `claim-rewards`: Withdraw earned tokens after validation threshold met
- `transfer-tokens`: Send tokens to other researchers
- `update-dataset-access`: Modify dataset visibility settings
- `access-dataset`: Record and retrieve dataset information
- `add-to-reward-pool`: Admin function to replenish rewards (owner only)
- `set-base-reward`: Admin function to adjust reward amounts (owner only)
- `set-validation-threshold`: Admin function to modify validation requirements (owner only)

### Read-Only Functions
- `get-dataset-info`: Retrieve complete dataset details
- `get-researcher-profile`: Access researcher information
- `get-researcher-balance`: Check token balance
- `get-validation-score`: View dataset validation metrics
- `has-validated`: Check if a validator reviewed a specific dataset
- `get-total-datasets`: Count total registered datasets
- `get-category-stats`: Access category-level statistics
- `get-pending-rewards`: Check unclaimed rewards
- `get-reward-pool`: View available reward balance
- `get-base-reward`: Check current base reward amount
- `get-validation-threshold`: View current validation threshold
- `get-access-log`: Retrieve access history for datasets
- `is-dataset-active`: Check dataset status
- `get-contract-owner`: View contract administrator

## Security Considerations

- Dataset ownership is immutable once registered
- Only dataset contributors can modify access settings
- Researchers cannot validate their own datasets
- Each validator can only review a dataset once
- Minimum claim interval prevents reward farming
- Administrative functions restricted to contract deployer
- Input validation on all public functions

## Testing Recommendations

1. Test dataset registration across all six categories
2. Verify validation restrictions (self-validation, duplicate validation)
3. Confirm reward calculation with different validation scores
4. Test claim interval enforcement
5. Verify access control on private datasets
6. Test token transfer between researchers
7. Validate administrative function restrictions
8. Check profile initialization on first interaction

## Integration Points

- Compatible with standard Stacks wallet integrations
- Ready for frontend dashboard development
- Supports analytics and reporting via read-only functions
- Extensible for future cross-contract interactions

## Future Enhancements

- Multi-signature validation for high-value datasets

## Summary
This PR introduces a complete notification system that allows users to schedule and receive notifications about tracked TV shows and movies releasing on specific dates. The system supports Discord webhooks as the initial provider and includes timezone-aware scheduling.

## Key Changes

### Frontend
- **NotificationsSection component** in ProfilePage: New UI for managing notifiers with create, edit, delete, test, and enable/disable functionality
- **Timezone support**: Automatic detection of user's timezone with fallback to common timezones
- **Form management**: Add/edit notifier form with provider selection, webhook URL input, time scheduling, and timezone selection
- **API integration**: New API methods for CRUD operations on notifiers and provider discovery

### Backend - Database
- **notifiers table**: New schema with fields for provider, name, config, notify_time, timezone, enabled status, and last_sent_date tracking
- **Repository functions**: CRUD operations for notifiers with user ownership enforcement
- **Query functions**: `getDueNotifiers()` to find notifiers ready to send, `getDistinctNotifierTimezones()` for job scheduling

### Backend - Notifications
- **NotificationProvider interface**: Extensible provider system with validation and send methods
- **DiscordProvider implementation**: Validates Discord webhook URLs and sends formatted embeds with episode/movie information
- **Content builder**: `buildNotificationContent()` aggregates tracked episodes and movies releasing on a given date
- **Types**: Structured types for notification content, episodes, movies, and providers

### Backend - Jobs
- **Notification job handler**: Runs periodically to check for due notifiers across all timezones
- **Timezone-aware scheduling**: Computes current time in each notifier's timezone to determine when to send
- **Deduplication**: Tracks last_sent_date to prevent duplicate notifications on the same day

### Backend - Routes
- **Notifiers API**: GET (list), POST (create), PUT (update), DELETE endpoints with ownership validation
- **Provider discovery**: GET /notifiers/providers endpoint
- **Test endpoint**: POST /:id/test for sending test notifications with sample content

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Timezone handling**: Uses Intl API for accurate timezone conversion with fallback list for unsupported environments
- **Ownership enforcement**: All notifier operations scoped to authenticated user via userId checks
- **Extensible provider system**: Registry pattern allows easy addition of new notification providers (Slack, email, etc.)
- **Comprehensive testing**: Unit tests for Discord provider validation, notification content building, and job scheduling logic
- **Graceful degradation**: Test notifications show sample content if nothing is actually releasing today
- **Discord embed limits**: Respects Discord's 10-embed-per-message limit

Follow-up fixes to #836 (new package detection in release script):

## Summary
This PR introduces a reusable contextual help system on key web app pages so users can get in-place guidance without leaving their current workflow. It adds a consistent `HelpIcon` trigger and `HelpModal` dialog wrapper, then wires them into Dashboard, Nutrition, Workouts, Habits, Foods, and Weight History headers. Each modal provides page-specific guidance aligned to Pulse domain behavior (for example, AI-managed nutrition entry, workout flow, and weight trend interpretation). The goal is to reduce ambiguity in complex areas while keeping help discoverable and lightweight. The update also expands test coverage to verify modal behavior and page-level help content rendering.

## Key Changes
- Added reusable UI primitives:
  - `HelpIcon` component using a ghost `CircleHelp` button with accessible labeling and mobile-friendly 44px tap target.
  - `HelpModal` component wrapping `Dialog` with a standard title/content layout and scrollable body for long guidance.
- Added contextual help entry points in page headers for:
  - Dashboard
  - Nutrition
  - Workouts
  - Habits
  - Foods
  - Weight History
- Added/updated tests to cover:
  - Help icon open/close interactions.
  - Help modal rendering when open vs. closed.
  - Modal styling/class expectations for readability and constrained height.
  - Presence of page-specific help copy on each integrated screen.

## Technical Notes
- Help content is embedded close to each page header to keep guidance maintainable and domain-specific, while reusing a single modal/trigger implementation.
- `HelpModal` intentionally uses constrained, scrollable content (`max-h` + `overflow-y-auto`) to preserve usability on smaller viewports.
- `DialogContent` is rendered with `aria-describedby={undefined}` because the modal body is custom structured content rather than a single `DialogDescription`.
- Tests focus on user-observable behavior (button, dialog, heading/content) rather than implementation internals, which should make refactors safer.

author: bharatkrishna1999
body:
## Summary
Implements the Damodaran Excess Return (ROE-Book Value) valuation model for financial sector companies (banks, NBFCs, insurance). This model is more appropriate for financial firms than traditional DCF, as it values companies based on book value plus the present value of excess returns (ROE minus cost of equity).

## Key Changes

- **Financial sector detection**: Added `is_financial_sector()` class method and `_FINANCIAL_SECTORS_SET`/`_FINANCIAL_INDUSTRIES` constants to identify banks, financial services, NBFCs, and insurance companies by sector and industry classification.

- **Excess Return valuation engine**: Implemented `excess_return_valuation()` method that:
  - Extracts book value per share, ROE, and cost of equity (via CAPM)
  - Calculates historical ROE and book value growth rates
  - Projects excess returns over a configurable period (5-10 years)
  - Computes intrinsic value as: Book Value + PV(Excess Returns) + Terminal Value
  - Returns comprehensive metrics including margin trends and historical data

- **Frontend UI for Excess Return model**: Added `renderExcessReturnResult()` and supporting JavaScript functions to display:
  - Interactive sliders for ROE, Cost of Equity, and growth rate assumptions
  - Year-by-year projection table with historical context
  - Sensitivity analysis grid (ROE vs Cost of Equity)
  - Value breakdown visualization (Book Value vs Excess Returns)
  - Verdict banner indicating undervalued/fairly valued/overvalued status

- **Intelligent model selection**: Modified `/dcf-data` route to:
  - Check local sector classification first
  - Route financial stocks to excess return model instead of DCF
  - Perform secondary validation using yfinance sector/industry data
  - Fallback to DCF for non-financial companies

- **Investment verdict integration**: Updated long-term holding score and narrative generation to handle excess return model metrics (ROE, excess spread, book value growth) alongside traditional DCF metrics.

## Implementation Details

- Cost of Equity calculated via CAPM: Rf(7%) + β × Market Risk Premium(6%)
- Terminal value of excess returns uses simplified perpetuity when cost of equity exceeds growth threshold
- Historical ROE and book value data extracted from yfinance balance sheet and income statement
- Margin trend analysis reuses existing DCF logic for consistency
- All financial calculations include proper error handling and fallback mechanisms
- UI styling matches existing DCF result presentation for consistency

author: shaythegay13
body:
💡 **What:** 
Optimized the user data deletion flow in `app/api/user/delete/route.ts` by replacing the sequential `for...of` loop with `Promise.all` and `.map()`. This allows deleting rows from `tablesWithUserId` concurrently rather than one after another.

🎯 **Why:** 
The previous implementation suffered from an N+1 query issue, causing unnecessary network delays. Each database table deletion awaited the completion of the previous one, slowing down the entire process.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
Using a mock performance script to simulate 50ms network delays per query:
- **Baseline (sequential):** ~503ms
- **Optimized (concurrent):** ~101ms
- **Improvement:** ~80% reduction in execution time for the data purge step.

author: fw-bot
body:
Current behavior
---
When confirming 1 SO with 2 products with 1 BoM and 1 Rerouting Rule with 0 min/max, with warehouse rule pbm (2 steps: Pick then manufacture), it creates a picking transfer with only 1 MO attached.

Expected behavior
---
The picking transfer should have 2 MO's.

Steps to reproduce
---
1. Create 2 Products with different BoM's, keep per-product routes empty. 
2. Set reordering rules for both to route: Manufacture.
3. Go to warehouses config and set manufacture rule to 2 step (pick -> manufacture)
4. Confirm a SO with those 2 products.

Cause of the issue
---
If we don't have any Make-to-Order routes for a product, the Make-to-Stock default rule of the warehouse would be used. 
In such case, all MO's related to such OP (orderpoint/warehouse) would be linked into one picking. The stock.picking model uses related fields to compute product_ids, which calculates relation using next(...) in the ORM. This takes only the first MO's stock move and ignores the second, hence ignoring other production groups.

Fix
---
Instead of using related fields, use compute to access every relavent production ids.

---

## Summary

This PR adds a **clear button** (trash icon) to the session name edit form, allowing users to quickly empty the input field with a single click. This improves the UX when renaming sessions with long names.

## Problem

When editing a session name via the pencil icon, long session names force users to manually select-all and delete the text before typing a new name. This is frustrating and slow, especially for frequently renamed sessions.

## Solution

Added a clear button that:
- Uses the **trash icon** (same SVG as the existing PR URL clear button)
- Styled in **red** (`var(--color-error)`) matching the existing `pr-clear-btn` pattern
- **Only visible when the input has text** (`v-if="editNameValue"`)
- Clicking it **empties the input field only** — does NOT save (session names cannot be empty)
- After clearing, the input is **auto-focused** so the user can immediately start typing

author: stilla[bot]
body:
## Problem

The "Copy Customer Portal" action in the admin dashboard failed for team customers with:

```
PolarRequestValidationError: member_id is required for team customers.
```

The backend requires `member_id` when creating a customer session for a team customer. The dashboard was only passing `customer_id`.

## Fix

In the dashboard (`CustomersPage.tsx` and `CustomerContextView.tsx`), when the customer type is `team`, the customer portal session creation now:

1. Fetches the customer's members via `GET /v1/members/`
2. Finds the member with `role === 'owner'`
3. Passes their `id` as `member_id` in the `POST /v1/customer-sessions/` request

This keeps the API behavior strict (team customers still require a `member_id`) while making the dashboard UI transparent about which member to use.

author: gokhantos
body:
## Summary

Adds an AI Skill Generator feature that lets users describe a skill in plain text and have an LLM generate a complete, structured skill definition. The generation streams in real time via SSE, shows a structured preview on completion, and pre-fills the create form when the user accepts.

## Changes

**Backend**
- `src/web/routes/skills.ts` — New `POST /api/skills/generate` SSE endpoint; Zod validation on prompt (1–2000 chars); custom `GENERATE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` with `<request>`-delimited input to mitigate prompt injection; 60s server-side timeout via `AbortController`; `createSkillRoutes` now accepts optional `WebAppDeps` to access the agent system
- `src/skills/loader.ts` — Defense-in-depth: `createSkill` now validates the derived skill ID with `isValidSkillId` after `toSkillId` transform (catches edge-case names that sanitize to an invalid slug)
- `src/web/app.ts` — Pass `deps` to `createSkillRoutes(deps)`

**Frontend**
- `src/web/ui/views/skills/AiSkillGenerator.tsx` — New modal component: prompt textarea, 6 suggestion chips, real-time SSE streaming display, JSON parsing on completion, structured preview (name / description / content), "Use This Skill" pre-fills the create form, Stop/Retry/Cancel controls with `AbortController`, generic error messages (no raw server text)
- `src/web/ui/views/skills/Skills.tsx` — "AI Generate" button in header wires `AiSkillGenerator.onGenerated` → create form pre-fill flow

## Testing

- [ ] `bun run typecheck` passes
- [ ] `bun test` passes
- [ ] Open Skills page → click "AI Generate" → enter a prompt → generation streams in real-time → preview appears on completion
- [ ] "Use This Skill" closes modal and opens create form with fields pre-filled
- [ ] "Stop" button aborts the in-flight stream and returns to idle
- [ ] "Retry" / "Try Again" re-runs generation with the same prompt
- [ ] Submitting an empty prompt is disabled (button stays disabled)
- [ ] Prompt exceeding 2000 chars returns a 400 from the API
- [ ] Verify server timeout fires after 60s if the LLM stalls

## Notes

- The `POST /api/skills/generate` route is gated behind `deps` availability; if the agent system is not initialized it returns 503 gracefully.
- `createSkillRoutes` signature changed from `()` to `(deps?: WebAppDeps)` — callers that omit `deps` continue to work unchanged.
